knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sensitivity or Postoptimality Analysis
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition encompassing numerical perturbations and additions of variables or constraints to a linear program.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Sensitivity analysis, also called postoptimality analysis, investigates how the optimal solutions of a linear program vary when its numerical data are changed or when variables or constraints are introduced.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sensitivity, or postoptimality, analysis studies how LP optimal solutions vary after changes to numerical data or the addition of variables or constraints.
assumptions_latex: \text{A linear program and one or more numerical or structural modifications are under consideration.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Studying the resulting variation in optimal solutions constitutes sensitivity or postoptimality analysis.}

children.title: Perturbation Classes
children.top_down_role: Classification by the LP data blocks subjected to variation.

children.title: Right-Hand-Side Perturbations
children.top_down_role: Changes to resources, requirements, and balance vectors.

assumptions_latex: The baseline problem is \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ l\le x\le u\}\), with compatible finite-dimensional data.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Only the constraint right-hand side varies; the objective, matrix, and variable bounds remain fixed.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional equality-form LPs with explicit bounds.

source_refs.locator: 5.2. Global dependence on the right-hand side vector p. 212

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A right-hand-side perturbation is the parametric family \[P(\theta):\quad \min_x\ c^{\mathsf T}x\quad\text{subject to}\quad Ax=b+R\theta,\quad l\le x\le u,\] where \(\theta\in\Theta\subseteq\mathbb R^k\). The data \(A\), \(c\), \(l\), and \(u\) are fixed. Its feasible-set and value maps are \(F(\theta)=\{x:Ax=b+R\theta,\ l\le x\le u\}\) and \(v(\theta)=\inf_{x\in F(\theta)}c^{\mathsf T}x\), using \(+\infty\) when \(F(\theta)=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A right-hand-side perturbation changes resource or balance values while holding costs, structural coefficients, and variable bounds fixed.
knowledge_statements.title: Right-Hand-Side Perturbations

source_witnesses.locator: 5.2. Global dependence on the right-hand side vector p. 212

children.title: Objective-Coefficient Perturbations
children.top_down_role: Changes to costs, revenues, and objective weights.

assumptions_latex: The baseline feasible set is \(F=\{x:Ax=b,\ l\le x\le u\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Only the linear objective coefficients vary; the feasible set remains \(F\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear objective perturbations over a fixed polyhedron.

source_refs.locator: 5.4. Global dependence on the cost vector p. 216

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An objective-coefficient perturbation is the parametric family \[P(\theta):\quad \min_{x\in F}\ (c+C\theta)^{\mathsf T}x,\qquad \theta\in\Theta\subseteq\mathbb R^k,\] where \(A\), \(b\), \(l\), and \(u\) are fixed. The value and solution maps are \(v(\theta)=\inf_{x\in F}(c+C\theta)^{\mathsf T}x\) and \(S(\theta)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in F}(c+C\theta)^{\mathsf T}x\), respectively.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An objective-coefficient perturbation changes costs, revenues, or weights while preserving the feasible region.
knowledge_statements.title: Objective-Coefficient Perturbations

source_witnesses.locator: 5.4. Global dependence on the cost vector p. 216

children.title: Variable-Bound Perturbations
children.top_down_role: Changes to explicit lower and upper variable limits.

assumptions_latex: The structural data \(A\), \(b\), and \(c\) are fixed.
The componentwise bounds satisfy \(l(\theta)\le u(\theta)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Only the admissible coordinate intervals vary with the parameter.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional LPs with componentwise affine bounds.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 7. Sensitivity and Parametric Analyses p. 109

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A variable-bound perturbation is the family \[P(\theta):\quad \min_x\ c^{\mathsf T}x\quad\text{subject to}\quad Ax=b,\quad l+L\theta\le x\le u+U\theta,\] indexed by \(\theta\in\Theta\subseteq\mathbb R^k\), with inequalities interpreted componentwise. Infinite bound components may be retained provided their perturbations are zero. Feasibility requires \(l+L\theta\le u+U\theta\), but this coordinatewise condition alone need not ensure existence of an \(x\) satisfying \(Ax=b\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A variable-bound perturbation changes explicit lower or upper coordinate limits while keeping the objective and structural equations fixed.
knowledge_statements.title: Variable-Bound Perturbations

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 7. Sensitivity and Parametric Analyses p. 109

children.title: Constraint-Matrix Perturbations
children.top_down_role: Changes to technological and structural coefficients.

assumptions_latex: The dimensions of \(A+\mathcal A(\theta)\), \(x\), and \(b\) are compatible.
The vectors \(b\), \(c\), \(l\), and \(u\) are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Technological coefficients vary, so both feasibility geometry and basis inverses may change.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine perturbations of finite-dimensional constraint matrices.

source_refs.locator: 2. Parametric Analysis and the Homotopy Method p. 113

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A constraint-matrix perturbation is the family \[P(\theta):\quad \min_x\ c^{\mathsf T}x\quad\text{subject to}\quad \left(A+\sum_{j=1}^k\theta_jA_j\right)x=b,\quad l\le x\le u,\] for \(\theta\in\Theta\subseteq\mathbb R^k\). Unlike a right-hand-side perturbation, it changes the linear map defining feasibility; consequently, even for a fixed column index set \(B\), the basic matrix \(A_B(\theta)\) and its nonsingularity can depend on \(\theta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constraint-matrix perturbation changes technological coefficients and can alter feasibility geometry, basis inverses, and basis validity.
knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Matrix Perturbations

source_witnesses.locator: 2. Parametric Analysis and the Homotopy Method p. 113

children.title: Mixed-Data Perturbation Coupling
children.top_down_role: Coordinated changes spanning multiple coefficients or data blocks.

children.title: Simultaneous Coefficient Perturbations
children.top_down_role: Coordinated changes to multiple coefficients within a common data block.

assumptions_latex: All affine data maps have compatible finite dimensions.
The parameter belongs to \(\Theta\subseteq\mathbb R^k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Two or more coefficient arrays vary under one shared parameter.

notation.meaning: affine parameterization of all LP data

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Shared-parameter affine perturbations of multiple LP coefficient arrays.

source_refs.locator: 6.8 Parametric Analysis p. 312

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A simultaneous coefficient perturbation is a family \[P(\theta):\quad \min_x\ c(\theta)^{\mathsf T}x\quad\text{subject to}\quad A(\theta)x=b(\theta),\quad l(\theta)\le x\le u(\theta),\] in which at least two maps among \(A(\theta)\), \(b(\theta)\), \(c(\theta)\), \(l(\theta)\), and \(u(\theta)\) are nonconstant. The same parameter \(\theta\) indexes every changing array, permitting their changes to occur simultaneously along a prescribed parameter direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A simultaneous perturbation varies at least two LP data arrays using a common parameter.
knowledge_statements.title: Simultaneous Coefficient Perturbations

source_witnesses.locator: 6.8 Parametric Analysis p. 312

children.title: Cross-Block Data Perturbations
children.top_down_role: Joint variation spanning distinct LP data blocks.

assumptions_latex: The LP data are partitioned into blocks \(D=(D_1,\ldots,D_q)\), where \(q\ge2\).
The parameter belongs to \(\Theta\subseteq\mathbb R^k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At least two distinct data blocks depend nontrivially on the parameter.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Blockwise classification of mixed LP data changes.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 7. Sensitivity and Parametric Analyses p. 109

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a block partition \(D=(D_1,\ldots,D_q)\) of the objective, right-hand side, matrix, and bound data, a cross-block data perturbation is a map \(\theta\mapsto D(\theta)\) for which \[\left|\left\{r:D_r(\theta)\ \text{is nonconstant on}\ \Theta\right\}\right|\ge2.\] Thus the perturbation crosses data-block boundaries, such as varying \(b(\theta)\) together with \(c(\theta)\), rather than changing several entries confined to one block.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cross-block perturbation changes data in at least two distinct classes, such as both right-hand sides and objective coefficients.
knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Block Data Perturbations

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 7. Sensitivity and Parametric Analyses p. 109

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed blockwise definition is mathematically coherent, but “cross-block data perturbation” is specialized taxonomy terminology and the cited general chapter locator does not establish that this exact classification or threshold is source-supported.

children.title: Coupled Perturbation Regimes
children.top_down_role: Parameter regimes shaped by dependencies among coordinated data changes.

knowledge_statements.title: Coupled Perturbation Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Non-Cartesian admissibility restrictions linking perturbations of multiple LP data blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Partition the LP data into blocks \(D=(D_1,\ldots,D_q)\), with blockwise perturbation spaces \(\mathcal Z_1,\ldots,\mathcal Z_q\). A coupled perturbation regime is an admissible set \[\mathcal U\subseteq\mathcal Z_1\times\cdots\times\mathcal Z_q\] involving at least two nonconstant block projections and satisfying \[\mathcal U\ne\operatorname{proj}_1(\mathcal U)\times\cdots\times\operatorname{proj}_q(\mathcal U).\] Thus admissibility in one varying block restricts admissibility in another. A shared parameterization \(D(\theta)\), \(\theta\in\Theta_c\), represents a coupled regime only when its image has this non-product property; for example, \(b(\theta)=b+R\theta\) and \(c(\theta)=c+C\theta\) driven by the same scalar parameter are coupled when both maps are nonconstant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A coupled perturbation regime links changes in at least two data blocks through joint restrictions, so the admissible changes are not the unrestricted product of their blockwise projections.
assumptions_latex: The LP data are partitioned into blocks \(D=(D_1,\ldots,D_q)\), where \(q\ge2\).
The admissible perturbation set \(\mathcal U\) is contained in the product of the blockwise perturbation spaces.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The regime is coupled when at least two block projections vary and \(\mathcal U\) is not the Cartesian product of all its blockwise projections.

notation.meaning: admissible set of joint block perturbations
projection of the admissible perturbation set onto block \(r\)

children.title: Local Basis Analysis
children.top_down_role: Perturbations preserving a selected optimal basis.

assumptions_latex: The LP is \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\), with \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) of row rank \(m\).
A selected index set \(B\) has \(|B|=m\) and nonsingular \(A_B\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selected basis remains optimal exactly while its basic variables and reduced costs retain the required signs.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard-form minimization with a fixed selected basis.

source_refs.locator: 5.1. Local sensitivity analysis p. 202

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For perturbed data \(A(\theta)\), \(b(\theta)\), and \(c(\theta)\), the fixed basis \(B\) is primal-dual optimal at \(\theta\) if and only if \[\det A_B(\theta)\ne0,\qquad A_B(\theta)^{-1}b(\theta)\ge0,\qquad c_N(\theta)-A_N(\theta)^{\mathsf T}A_B(\theta)^{-\mathsf T}c_B(\theta)\ge0.\] When these conditions hold, \(x_B(\theta)=A_B(\theta)^{-1}b(\theta)\), \(x_N(\theta)=0\), and the local value is \(v_B(\theta)=c_B(\theta)^{\mathsf T}A_B(\theta)^{-1}b(\theta)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Local basis analysis tracks primal feasibility, dual feasibility, and nonsingularity conditions that keep one selected basis optimal.
knowledge_statements.title: Local Basis Analysis

source_witnesses.locator: 5.1. Local sensitivity analysis p. 202

children.title: Regional Invariancy Analysis
children.top_down_role: Parameter regions preserving a basis, support set, partition, or optimal face.

knowledge_statements.title: Regional Invariancy Analysis
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polyhedral optimality regions for a fixed basis under fixed-matrix affine right-hand-side and objective perturbations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(b(\theta)=b+R\theta\), \(c(\theta)=c+C\theta\), and let \(\Theta\subseteq\mathbb R^k\) be polyhedral. For a fixed nonsingular basis \(B\), its regional invariancy set is \[\mathcal R_B=\left\{\theta\in\Theta:A_B^{-1}(b+R\theta)\ge0,\ (c_N+C_N\theta)-A_N^{\mathsf T}A_B^{-\mathsf T}(c_B+C_B\theta)\ge0\right\}.\] The set \(\mathcal R_B\) is polyhedral. On it, the basis remains primal-dual optimal, its basic/nonbasic partition is unchanged, and the basic solution is affine in \(\theta\). Alternative optimal bases may coexist where degeneracy or zero reduced costs occur.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a polyhedral parameter domain, the regional invariancy set of a fixed basis is the polyhedron of parameters satisfying its primal- and dual-feasibility inequalities.
assumptions_latex: The LP is in standard minimization form with fixed \(A\), and \(b(\theta)=b+R\theta\) and \(c(\theta)=c+C\theta\).
The selected basis matrix \(A_B\) is nonsingular.
The parameter domain \(\Theta\subseteq\mathbb R^k\) is polyhedral.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The fixed-basis invariancy region \(\mathcal R_B\) is a polyhedron defined by primal and dual sign inequalities.

children.title: Global Optimal-Dependence Regimes
children.top_down_role: Behavior across all relevant parameter regimes, including structural transitions.

children.title: Global Optimal-Value Dependence
children.top_down_role: Optimal-value behavior across the relevant parameter domain.

assumptions_latex: The primal family is \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\), with fixed \(A\) and \(c\).
At the considered \(b\), the primal is feasible and has finite value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The global value is the support function of the dual feasible polyhedron and is convex piecewise affine in \(b\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global right-hand-side value dependence in standard form.

source_refs.locator: 5.2. Global dependence on the right-hand side vector p. 212

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Strong duality gives the global representation \[v(b)=\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}=\max_{y\in Y}b^{\mathsf T}y,\qquad Y=\{y:A^{\mathsf T}y\le c\}.\] Hence \(v\) is convex and polyhedral on the set of right-hand sides for which the value is finite. On any region where one dual extreme point \(y^*\) is optimal, \(v(b)=b^{\mathsf T}y^*\); changes of the maximizing dual face produce the global breakpoints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Globally, the finite right-hand-side value function is the dual polyhedron's support function, hence convex and piecewise affine.
knowledge_statements.title: Global Optimal-Value Dependence

source_witnesses.locator: 5.2. Global dependence on the right-hand side vector p. 212

children.title: Global Optimal-Solution Dependence
children.top_down_role: Optimal-solution-set behavior across parameter regimes.

knowledge_statements.title: Global Optimal-Solution Dependence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-matrix affine right-hand-side and objective dependence, including possibly unbounded optimal faces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have row rank \(m\), let \(\mathcal B\) be its finite collection of nonsingular bases, and let \(\mathcal R_B\) be the parameter region where \(B\) is primal-dual optimal. For \(B\in\mathcal B\), define \[x^B_B(\theta)=A_B^{-1}b(\theta),\qquad x^B_N(\theta)=0.\] If the optimum at \(\theta\) is attained and finite, then \[S(\theta)=\operatorname{conv}\left\{x^B(\theta):B\in\mathcal B,\ \theta\in\mathcal R_B\right\}+K(\theta),\] where \[K(\theta)=\left\{d\in\mathbb R^n:Ad=0,\ d\ge0,\ c(\theta)^{\mathsf T}d=0\right\}.\] Thus the optimal extreme-point branches are affine, while multiple optimal bases can make the map set-valued and nonzero vectors in \(K(\theta)\) can make the optimal face unbounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The global optimizer set is the convex hull of its affine optimal basic-solution branches plus any zero-cost feasible recession directions.
assumptions_latex: The family is \(\min\{c(\theta)^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b(\theta),\ x\ge0\}\), where \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) is fixed and has row rank \(m\).
The maps \(b(\theta)\) and \(c(\theta)\) are affine.
For every considered \(\theta\), the optimum is attained and finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The optimizer set is the convex hull of all optimal basic solutions plus the cone of zero-cost feasible recession directions.

notation.meaning: zero-cost recession cone of the optimal face

source_refs.locator: 6.8 Parametric Analysis p. 312

source_witnesses.locator: 6.8 Parametric Analysis p. 312

children.title: Structural Transition Regimes
children.top_down_role: Parameter regions where the applicable optimal structure changes.

assumptions_latex: The LP data depend continuously on \(\theta\).
On an open parameter region, a basis \(B\) is nonsingular and satisfies strict primal and dual inequalities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A structural transition can occur only when nonsingularity or a strict primal-dual basis inequality is lost.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary mechanisms for changes of an optimal basis.

source_refs.locator: 1. Sensitivity Analysis p. 109
5.1. Local sensitivity analysis p. 202

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a currently optimal basis \(B\), its strict invariancy regime ends only at a parameter satisfying at least one boundary equation \[\det A_B(\theta)=0,\qquad x_{B,i}(\theta)=0\ \text{for some}\ i\in B,\qquad \bar c_j(\theta)=0\ \text{for some}\ j\notin B.\] These events respectively mark loss of the basis, loss of strict primal feasibility, or loss of strict dual feasibility. Crossing such a boundary may change the optimal basis, active partition, optimal face, or feasibility and boundedness status.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Structural transitions occur where a basis becomes singular, a basic variable reaches zero, or a reduced cost reaches zero.
knowledge_statements.title: Structural Transition Regimes

children.title: Optimal-Basis Representation
children.top_down_role: Classical organization through a selected simplex basis.

knowledge_statements.title: Optimal-Basis Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard-form minimization with a selected simplex basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\mathcal N=\{1,\ldots,n\}\setminus\mathcal B\), define \(y^*=B^{-T}c_{\mathcal B}\) and \(\bar c_{\mathcal N}=c_{\mathcal N}-A_{:,\mathcal N}^Ty^*\). The basis \(\mathcal B\) is optimal exactly when \(B^{-1}b\geq0\) and \(\bar c_{\mathcal N}\geq0\). It then represents a primal-dual optimal pair by \(x^*_{\mathcal B}=B^{-1}b\), \(x^*_{\mathcal N}=0\), and \(y^*=B^{-T}c_{\mathcal B}\), with optimal value \(c^Tx^*=b^Ty^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An invertible basis represents an optimum precisely when its basic solution and nonbasic reduced costs are nonnegative; the basis equations then give primal and dual optimizers.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) has rank \(m\), \(\mathcal B\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) has cardinality \(m\), and \(B=A_{:,\mathcal B}\) is nonsingular.
Consider the standard-form problem \(\min\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ x\geq0\}\), where \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\) and \(c\in\mathbb{R}^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^*_{\mathcal B}=B^{-1}b\), \(x^*_{\mathcal N}=0\), and \(v=b^TB^{-T}c_{\mathcal B}\).

source_refs.locator: Chapter 7. Sensitivity and Parametric Analyses p. 109

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 7. Sensitivity and Parametric Analyses p. 109

children.title: Optimal Face-Normal Cone Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Basis-independent organization through primal optimal faces and objective-space regions.

children.title: Optimal-Face Geometry
children.top_down_role: Primal geometric organization through optimal faces.

assumptions_latex: \(P\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is a nonempty polyhedron.
The linear program \(\min\{c^Tx:x\in P\}\) has a finite attained value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F^*(c)=P\cap\{x:c^Tx=v(c)\}\) is an exposed face of \(P\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional polyhedral geometry for a fixed linear objective.

source_refs.locator: 5.3. The set of all dual optimal solutions* p. 215

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(v(c)=\min_{x\in P}c^Tx\). The optimizer set satisfies \[F^*(c)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in P}c^Tx=P\cap\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:c^Tx=v(c)\}.\] Thus \(F^*(c)\) is a nonempty exposed face of \(P\). Every point of \(\operatorname{relint}F^*(c)\) lies in exactly the same minimal face of \(P\), so active-constraint changes within the relative interior do not change the optimal face.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The minimizers of an attained polyhedral linear program form the exposed face cut out by the objective’s supporting hyperplane.
knowledge_statements.title: Optimal-Face Geometry

source_witnesses.locator: 5.3. The set of all dual optimal solutions* p. 215

children.title: Normal-Cone Geometry
children.top_down_role: Objective-space organization through normal cones.

assumptions_latex: \(P\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is a nonempty polyhedron.
\(F\) is a nonempty face of \(P\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_P(F)\) is a polyhedral cone constant on \(\operatorname{relint}F\).

notation.meaning: Minimization normal cone of P along F

knowledge_statements.scope_note: The normal-cone sign convention is chosen for minimization objectives.

source_refs.locator: 5.3. The set of all dual optimal solutions* p. 215

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The minimization normal cone of \(P\) along \(F\) is \[N_P(F)=\{c\in\mathbb{R}^n:c^T(y-x)\geq0\ \text{for every }x\in F\text{ and }y\in P\}.\] Equivalently, \(c\in N_P(F)\) exactly when every point of \(F\) minimizes \(c^Tx\) over \(P\). This is a closed polyhedral convex cone, and for every \(x\in\operatorname{relint}F\), the pointwise normal cone \(N_P(x)\) equals \(N_P(F)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A face’s minimization normal cone consists of all objective vectors for which every point of that face is optimal.
knowledge_statements.title: Normal-Cone Geometry

source_witnesses.locator: 5.3. The set of all dual optimal solutions* p. 215

children.title: Face–Cone Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Association between primal optimal faces and objective-space regions.

assumptions_latex: \(P\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is a nonempty polyhedron.
\(F\) and \(G\) are nonempty faces of \(P\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in P}c^Tx\) exactly when \(c\in\operatorname{relint}N_P(F)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correspondence between exposed faces and relative interiors of minimization normal cones.

source_refs.locator: 5.3. The set of all dual optimal solutions* p. 215

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every objective \(c\) whose minimum over \(P\) is attained, \[F=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in P}c^Tx\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad c\in\operatorname{relint}N_P(F).\] Moreover, face inclusion reverses normal-cone inclusion: \[F\subseteq G\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad N_P(G)\subseteq N_P(F).\] Hence objectives in one relative-open normal-cone cell select the same optimal face, while crossing a cone boundary enlarges or changes the selected face.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each normal-cone relative interior selects exactly one optimal face, and inclusion of faces reverses inclusion of their normal cones.
knowledge_statements.title: Face–Cone Correspondence

source_witnesses.locator: 5.3. The set of all dual optimal solutions* p. 215

children.top_down_role: Organization through the primal-dual partition and complementary structure.

assumptions_latex: The primal-dual pair is \(\min\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ x\geq0\}\) and \(\max\{b^Ty:A^Ty+s=c,\ s\geq0\}\).
Both problems have optimal solutions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal B\cap\mathcal N=\varnothing\), \(\mathcal B\cup\mathcal N=\{1,\ldots,n\}\), and relative-interior optima have supports \(\mathcal B\) and \(\mathcal N\).

notation.meaning: Indices positive in some primal optimum
Indices with positive slack in some dual optimum

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimal partition induced by complementary primal variables and dual slacks.

source_refs.locator: 6.2 Primal-Dual Relationships p. 264

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(\mathcal B=\{i:x_i>0\text{ for some primal optimum }x\}\) and \(\mathcal N=\{i:s_i>0\text{ for some dual optimum }(y,s)\}\). Complementarity and strict complementarity imply \(\mathcal B\cap\mathcal N=\varnothing\) and \(\mathcal B\cup\mathcal N=\{1,\ldots,n\}\). Every relative-interior primal optimum satisfies \(x_i>0\) exactly for \(i\in\mathcal B\), and every relative-interior dual slack satisfies \(s_i>0\) exactly for \(i\in\mathcal N\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strict complementarity partitions indices into those supported by primal optima and those supported by dual optimal slacks; relative-interior optima realize the entire partition.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Dual Optimal-Partition Representation

knowledge_statements.title: Invariant Support-Set Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Support invariance is defined using relative-interior optimal solutions to avoid selection ambiguity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\), define \[\mathcal R_S=\{\theta\in\Theta:\operatorname{supp}(x)=S\text{ for every }x\in\operatorname{relint}X^*(\theta)\}.\] This is well defined because, for any nonempty convex set \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}_+^n\), all points of \(\operatorname{relint}C\) have the same support, equal to the union of the supports of points in \(C\). On \(\mathcal R_S\), the indices that can be positive in an optimal solution are invariant and equal \(S\), although the optimal point and optimal value may vary with \(\theta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A parameter region has invariant optimal support when relative-interior optimal solutions have the same positive-coordinate set throughout that region.
assumptions_latex: For each parameter \(\theta\in\Theta\subseteq\mathbb{R}^q\), \(X^*(\theta)\) is a nonempty optimal face of a standard-form linear program and hence is a convex subset of \(\mathbb{R}_+^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal R_S=\{\theta\in\Theta:\operatorname{supp}(x)=S\text{ for every }x\in\operatorname{relint}X^*(\theta)\}\) represents the parameter set with invariant optimal support \(S\).

notation.meaning: Optimal solution set at parameter theta

children.title: Parametric Value Functions
children.top_down_role: Functional representation of optimal values over parameter space.

assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) and \(c\in\mathbb{R}^n\) are fixed.
For the right-hand side \(b\), the primal value is finite and the feasible set is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v(b)=\max\{b^Ty:A^Ty\leq c\}\), so \(v\) is convex and polyhedral on its effective domain.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Right-hand-side parametric standard-form linear programming.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 7. Sensitivity and Parametric Analyses p. 109
6.2 Primal-Dual Relationships p. 264

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the extended value function by \[v(b)=\inf\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ x\geq0\},\] with \(v(b)=+\infty\) when the constraints are infeasible. Whenever \(v(b)\) is finite, linear-programming duality gives \[v(b)=\max\{b^Ty:A^Ty\leq c\}.\] Consequently, \(v\) is a convex polyhedral function of \(b\); on every region where one dual extreme point remains optimal, \(v\) is affine with that dual solution as a slope.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The right-hand-side value equals the maximum of dual affine functions, making it convex, polyhedral, and locally affine on fixed-dual-solution regions.
knowledge_statements.title: Parametric Value Functions

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Piecewise-Linear Parametric LP Value Function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded theorem for the one-parameter linear program denoted (10.28) in the source; that program's defining formulation is outside this extract.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let P(p) denote the parametric linear program (10.28). If P(p_0) has an optimal solution for some parameter value p_0, then there exist k\ge 1, coefficients r_i,s_i\in\mathbb{R} for i=1,\ldots,k, and an interval I such that P(p) is infeasible for every p\notin I, whereas for every p\in I, P(p) has an optimal solution and z^*(p)=\min_{1\le i\le k}(r_i+s_i p).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the source's one-parameter linear program has an optimal solution for at least one parameter value, then there is an interval I outside which the program is infeasible and on which it always has an optimal solution. Its optimal value on I is the minimum of finitely many affine functions of the parameter.
assumptions_latex: \exists p_0\in\mathbb{R}\text{ such that }P(p_0)\text{ has an optimal solution}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists k\ge1,\ \{(r_i,s_i)\}_{i=1}^k\subset\mathbb{R}^2,\ I\text{ an interval}:\quad p\notin I\Rightarrow P(p)\text{ is infeasible},\qquad p\in I\Rightarrow P(p)\text{ has an optimal solution and }z^*(p)=\min_{1\le i\le k}(r_i+s_i p).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite Affine-Envelope Value Function for a Scalar Parametric LP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimal-value representation and unboundedness boundary for an LP with a fixed feasible region and scalar-affine objective coefficients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a scalar objective-parametric LP with a feasible region independent of \(p\) and an objective affine in \(p\). If it has an optimal solution for at least one value of \(p\), then there exist finitely many affine functions \(r_1+s_1p,\ldots,r_k+s_kp\) and an interval \(I\) such that: (i) if \(p\notin I\), the LP is unbounded; and (ii) if \(p\in I\), the LP has an optimal solution with value \(z^*(p)=\max_{1\le i\le k}(r_i+s_ip)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If an LP with a fixed feasible region and scalar-affine objective has an optimum for at least one parameter value, the parameter values admitting finite optima form an interval. Outside it the LP is unbounded; inside it the optimal value is the maximum of finitely many affine functions.
assumptions_latex: \text{The feasible region is independent of the scalar parameter }p.
\text{The objective coefficients depend affinely on }p.
\exists p_0\;\text{such that the parametric LP has an optimal solution at }p_0.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists I,\,k<\infty,\,(r_i,s_i)_{i=1}^k:\quad p\notin I\Rightarrow\text{unbounded},\qquad p\in I\Rightarrow z^*(p)=\max_{1\le i\le k}(r_i+s_ip).

children.title: Parametric Solution Mappings
children.top_down_role: Set-valued representation of optimal solutions over parameter space.

assumptions_latex: The data \(A(\theta)\), \(b(\theta)\), and \(c(\theta)\) define a linear program for each \(\theta\in\Theta\).
The infimum is attained whenever the value \(v(\theta)\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X^*(\theta)=\{x\geq0:A(\theta)x=b(\theta),\ c(\theta)^Tx=v(\theta)\}\).

notation.meaning: Set of optimal solutions at theta

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set-valued optimizer mapping for a parameterized standard-form linear program.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 7. Sensitivity and Parametric Analyses p. 109

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \[v(\theta)=\inf\{c(\theta)^Tx:A(\theta)x=b(\theta),\ x\geq0\}.\] The parametric solution mapping is \[X^*(\theta)=\operatorname*{argmin}\{c(\theta)^Tx:A(\theta)x=b(\theta),\ x\geq0\}=\{x\geq0:A(\theta)x=b(\theta),\ c(\theta)^Tx=v(\theta)\}.\] It is empty when the infimum is not attained. When nonempty, each value \(X^*(\theta)\) is a polyhedral face of the feasible set at \(\theta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The parametric solution mapping assigns each parameter all feasible points whose objective equals the parameterized optimal value.
knowledge_statements.title: Parametric Solution Mappings

children.title: Function–Mapping Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Connections between value regimes and solution-set regimes.

assumptions_latex: \(v(b)=\min\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ x\geq0\}\) is finite and attained.
The dual feasible set \(D=\{y:A^Ty\leq c\}\) is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X^*(b)=\{x\geq0:Ax=b,\ c^Tx=v(b)\}\) and \(\partial v(b)=Y^*(b)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Right-hand-side value function and its primal and dual optimizer mappings.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 7. Sensitivity and Parametric Analyses p. 109
6.2 Primal-Dual Relationships p. 264

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(Y^*(b)=\operatorname*{argmax}_{y\in D}b^Ty\). Strong duality yields \[X^*(b)=\{x\geq0:Ax=b,\ c^Tx=v(b)\}.\] Because \(v(b)=\max_{y\in D}b^Ty\), the active affine slopes are precisely the dual optimizers, and hence \[\partial v(b)=Y^*(b).\] Thus the value function records the common objective level of the primal solution mapping, while its subdifferential records the dual solution mapping.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Primal optimizers are feasible points on the value level set, while the value function’s subgradients are exactly the optimal dual multipliers.
knowledge_statements.title: Function–Mapping Correspondence

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Linear-Programming Sensitivity Analysis
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines LP sensitivity analysis generally and identifies the section’s classical local focus on coefficient ranges preserving optimality and objective-value sensitivity near an optimal vertex.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a linear program with data coefficients \(a_{ij}\), \(b_i\), and \(c_j\), sensitivity analysis investigates changes in the optimum resulting from changes in these data. In classical local ranging analysis, it determines the range of a specified data element over which the solution of the original problem remains optimal; it may also examine the sensitivity of the objective function to an implicit parameter near an optimal vertex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sensitivity analysis investigates how changes in a linear program’s constraint coefficients, right-hand sides, or objective coefficients change the optimum. In classical local ranging analysis, it determines the range of a specified data element for which the original problem’s solution remains optimal and may also study objective-function sensitivity near an optimal vertex.
assumptions_latex: \text{The optimization problem is a linear program with data }(a_{ij},b_i,c_j).
\text{At least one specified data element is allowed to vary.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Sensitivity analysis characterizes changes in the optimum and, locally, ranges of data values that preserve optimality of the original solution.}

children.title: Basis-Stability Structure
children.top_down_role: The primal and dual conditions governing persistence of a reference basis.

children.title: Primal-Feasibility Stability
children.top_down_role: Persistence of basic feasibility under RHS and bound changes.

assumptions_latex: \(B=A_{:,\mathcal B}\) is a fixed nonsingular basis.
Nonbasic variables remain fixed at their selected lower or upper bounds under the perturbation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The basis remains primal feasible exactly when its updated basic vector lies between its updated bounds.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-basis feasibility under simultaneous right-hand-side and variable-bound changes.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 7. Sensitivity and Parametric Analyses p. 109

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the perturbed constraints be \(Ax=b+\Delta b\) with bounds \(l+\Delta l\leq x\leq u+\Delta u\), and let \(\widehat x_{\mathcal N}\) contain the perturbed bounds selected for the nonbasic variables. The fixed basis determines \[\widehat x_{\mathcal B}=B^{-1}\bigl(b+\Delta b-A_{:,\mathcal N}\widehat x_{\mathcal N}\bigr).\] It remains primal feasible exactly when \[l_{\mathcal B}+\Delta l_{\mathcal B}\leq\widehat x_{\mathcal B}\leq u_{\mathcal B}+\Delta u_{\mathcal B},\] together with validity of every selected nonbasic bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under right-hand-side and bound changes, a fixed basis stays feasible exactly while its recomputed basic variables remain within their perturbed bounds.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Feasibility Stability

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 7. Sensitivity and Parametric Analyses p. 109

children.title: Objective-Side Basis Stability
children.top_down_role: Persistence of basis optimality under objective changes.

children.title: Dual-Feasibility Stability
children.top_down_role: Persistence of dual feasibility under objective-data variation.

assumptions_latex: \(B=A_{:,\mathcal B}\) is a fixed nonsingular basis for a standard-form minimization problem.
The objective changes from \(c\) to \(c+\Delta c\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The basis remains dual feasible exactly when \(A^T\widehat y\leq c+\Delta c\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual feasibility of a fixed simplex basis under objective-coefficient perturbations.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 7. Sensitivity and Parametric Analyses p. 109

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The perturbed basic dual equations determine \[\widehat y=B^{-T}(c_{\mathcal B}+\Delta c_{\mathcal B}).\] Define the perturbed dual slack by \(\widehat s=c+\Delta c-A^T\widehat y\). Its basic components vanish. The fixed basis remains dual feasible exactly when \[\widehat s_{\mathcal N}=c_{\mathcal N}+\Delta c_{\mathcal N}-A_{:,\mathcal N}^TB^{-T}(c_{\mathcal B}+\Delta c_{\mathcal B})\geq0,\] equivalently when \(A^T\widehat y\leq c+\Delta c\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed basis remains dual feasible under objective changes precisely when the dual multiplier induced by its perturbed basic costs satisfies every dual inequality.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Feasibility Stability

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 7. Sensitivity and Parametric Analyses p. 109

children.title: Reduced-Cost Stability
children.top_down_role: Persistence of reduced-cost status under objective-data variation.

assumptions_latex: \(B=A_{:,\mathcal B}\) is a fixed nonsingular basis for \(\min\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ x\geq0\}\).
The objective perturbation is \(\Delta c\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat{\bar c}_{\mathcal N}=\bar c_{\mathcal N}+\Delta c_{\mathcal N}-A_{:,\mathcal N}^TB^{-T}\Delta c_{\mathcal B}\), and stability is equivalent to \(\widehat{\bar c}_{\mathcal N}\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine reduced-cost update for a fixed basis in standard-form minimization.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 7. Sensitivity and Parametric Analyses p. 109

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: With \(\bar c_{\mathcal N}=c_{\mathcal N}-A_{:,\mathcal N}^TB^{-T}c_{\mathcal B}\), the objective perturbation produces \[\widehat{\bar c}_{\mathcal N}=\bar c_{\mathcal N}+\Delta c_{\mathcal N}-A_{:,\mathcal N}^TB^{-T}\Delta c_{\mathcal B}.\] Thus reduced-cost signs remain compatible with optimality exactly when \(\widehat{\bar c}_{\mathcal N}\geq0\). The stability region in \(\Delta c\)-space is therefore a polyhedron; its boundary is reached when at least one perturbed nonbasic reduced cost equals zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reduced costs vary affinely with objective perturbations, and their componentwise nonnegativity defines the fixed basis’s objective-side stability region.
knowledge_statements.title: Reduced-Cost Stability

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 7. Sensitivity and Parametric Analyses p. 109

children.title: Objective-Perturbation Stability Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Limits at which dual or reduced-cost status changes.

assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) has full row rank, and \(B=A_{[:,\mathcal B]}\) is nonsingular.
The reference basis is primal feasible and optimal for \(\min\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ x\ge 0\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal S_c=\{d\in\mathbb R^n:r_N+d_N-N^TB^{-T}d_B\ge0\}\), with boundary contained in \(\bigcup_{j\in\mathcal N}\{d:(r_N+d_N-N^TB^{-T}d_B)_j=0\}\).

notation.meaning: Nonbasic reduced-cost vector for the reference basis.
Objective-coefficient perturbation partitioned by the basis.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimization-form boundary for a fixed standard-form basis.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 7. Sensitivity and Parametric Analyses p. 109

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an objective perturbation \(c\mapsto c+d\), the reference basic solution is unchanged and its reduced costs become \(r_N(d)=r_N+d_N-N^TB^{-T}d_B\). The basis remains optimal exactly while \(r_N(d)\ge0\). Hence its objective-stability region is the polyhedron \(\mathcal S_c=\{d:r_N(d)\ge0\}\). A stability boundary is reached when at least one inequality is tight, namely \(r_j(d)=0\) for some \(j\in\mathcal N\); crossing that facet makes the corresponding reduced cost negative and destroys optimality of the reference basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Objective perturbations preserve the reference basis exactly while every perturbed nonbasic reduced cost remains nonnegative; stability boundaries occur when one becomes zero.
knowledge_statements.title: Objective-Perturbation Stability Boundaries

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 7. Sensitivity and Parametric Analyses p. 109

children.title: Joint Primal-Dual Basis Stability
children.top_down_role: Combined perturbations constrained by both feasibility and optimality.

assumptions_latex: \(B=A_{[:,\mathcal B]}\) is a nonsingular reference basis for a standard-form minimization LP.
The right-hand side and objective are perturbed to \(b+h\) and \(c+d\), while \(A\) is fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B^{-1}(b+h)\ge0\quad\text{and}\quad c_N+d_N-N^TB^{-T}(c_B+d_B)\ge0\).

notation.meaning: Objective perturbation partitioned into basic and nonbasic components.
Reference basis matrix and complementary nonbasic matrix.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact fixed-basis conditions under simultaneous RHS and objective changes.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 7. Sensitivity and Parametric Analyses p. 109
11-1. Complementary Primal and Dual Bases p. 241

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min\{(c+d)^Tx:Ax=b+h,\ x\ge0\}\), the reference basis defines \(x_B(h)=B^{-1}(b+h)\), \(x_N=0\), and dual vector \(y(d)=B^{-T}(c_B+d_B)\). It is simultaneously primal feasible and dual feasible, hence optimal, if and only if \(B^{-1}(b+h)\ge0\) and \(c_N+d_N-N^Ty(d)\ge0\). Thus the joint stability set is the intersection of the primal-feasibility inequalities in \(h\) and the reduced-cost inequalities in \(d\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed basis survives combined RHS and objective changes exactly when its perturbed basic variables and nonbasic reduced costs are both nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.title: Joint Primal-Dual Basis Stability

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 7. Sensitivity and Parametric Analyses p. 109
11-1. Complementary Primal and Dual Bases p. 241

children.title: Resource-Side Feasibility Ranges
children.top_down_role: Local feasibility ranges and associated valuation regimes.

children.title: Single-RHS Feasibility Ranges
children.top_down_role: Allowable variation of an individual RHS component.

assumptions_latex: \(B\) is a nonsingular feasible basis with \(x_B^0=B^{-1}b\ge0\).
Only right-hand-side component \(b_i\) changes, by \(\theta\in\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\theta\in\bigcap_{k=1}^m\{\theta:x_{B,k}^0+\theta(B^{-1})_{ki}\ge0\}\).

notation.meaning: The ith coordinate vector in right-hand-side space.
Scalar change in the selected RHS component.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact allowable interval for one RHS coordinate and a fixed basis.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 7. Sensitivity and Parametric Analyses p. 109

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under \(b\mapsto b+\theta e_i\), the reference basis produces \(x_B(\theta)=x_B^0+\theta B^{-1}e_i\). Its exact feasibility range is \(I_i=\{\theta:x_B^0+\theta B^{-1}e_i\ge0\}\), an interval containing \(0\). Equivalently, every row \(k\) imposes \(x_{B,k}^0+\theta(B^{-1})_{ki}\ge0\). Rows with positive coefficients give lower bounds on \(\theta\), rows with negative coefficients give upper bounds, and rows with zero coefficients impose no new restriction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The allowable change in one RHS entry is the interval on which every affine basic-variable value remains nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.title: Single-RHS Feasibility Ranges

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 7. Sensitivity and Parametric Analyses p. 109

children.title: RHS Marginal-Value Validity Ranges
children.top_down_role: Ranges over which a reported resource valuation remains associated with the reference structure.

assumptions_latex: The reference basis \(B\) is optimal for \(\min\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\).
Only \(b_i\) is changed by \(\theta\), and the reference basis remains feasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v(b+\theta e_i)=v(b)+\theta y_i\), where \(y=B^{-T}c_B\).

notation.meaning: Optimal value as a function of the right-hand side.
Dual-price vector associated with the reference basis.
Allowable perturbation of RHS component i.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-basis interval on which one reported shadow price remains valid.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 7. Sensitivity and Parametric Analyses p. 109

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(y=B^{-T}c_B\) be the dual vector of the reference optimal basis. For every \(\theta\) in the single-RHS feasibility range \(I_i=\{\theta:B^{-1}(b+\theta e_i)\ge0\}\), objective coefficients are unchanged, so the basis remains optimal and \(v(b+\theta e_i)=c_B^TB^{-1}(b+\theta e_i)=v(b)+\theta y_i\). Thus the reported marginal value \(y_i\) is valid throughout \(I_i\), although another optimal basis may coexist at degenerate points.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reported shadow price remains the exact value slope throughout the RHS interval where the reference basis stays feasible.
knowledge_statements.title: RHS Marginal-Value Validity Ranges

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 7. Sensitivity and Parametric Analyses p. 109

children.title: Variable-Bound Range Pair
children.top_down_role: Ranges for explicit variable limits in bounded-variable formulations.

children.title: Lower-Bound Ranges
children.top_down_role: Allowable variation associated with explicit lower variable limits.

assumptions_latex: Consider \(\min\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ l\le x\le u\}\) with a fixed optimal bounded-variable basis \(B\).
A nonbasic variable \(x_j=l_j\) remains assigned to its lower bound while \(l_j\mapsto l_j+\theta\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\theta\in\{\theta:l_B\le x_B^0-\theta B^{-1}A_j\le u_B,\ l_j+\theta\le u_j\}\).

notation.meaning: Reference values of the basic variables.
Column of A belonging to the lower-bound nonbasic variable.
Change in the selected lower bound.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bounded-variable simplex range for a nonbasic variable at its lower bound.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 7. Sensitivity and Parametric Analyses p. 109

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Changing the active lower bound to \(l_j+\theta\) fixes \(x_j=l_j+\theta\) and changes the basic solution to \(x_B(\theta)=x_B^0-\theta B^{-1}A_j\). The lower-bound stability range is exactly the interval of \(\theta\) satisfying \(l_B\le x_B(\theta)\le u_B\) together with \(l_j+\theta\le u_j\). Because the objective and active-bound status are fixed, reduced costs do not change; consequently the reference bounded-variable basis remains optimal throughout this feasibility interval.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lower-bound change is allowable while the induced affine basic solution respects all bounds and the modified lower bound does not exceed its upper bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Lower-Bound Ranges

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 7. Sensitivity and Parametric Analyses p. 109

children.title: Upper-Bound Ranges
children.top_down_role: Allowable variation associated with explicit upper variable limits.

assumptions_latex: Consider \(\min\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ l\le x\le u\}\) with a fixed optimal bounded-variable basis \(B\).
A nonbasic variable \(x_j=u_j\) remains assigned to its upper bound while \(u_j\mapsto u_j+\theta\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\theta\in\{\theta:l_B\le x_B^0-\theta B^{-1}A_j\le u_B,\ l_j\le u_j+\theta\}\).

notation.meaning: Reference values of the basic variables.
Column of A belonging to the upper-bound nonbasic variable.
Change in the selected upper bound.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bounded-variable simplex range for a nonbasic variable at its upper bound.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 7. Sensitivity and Parametric Analyses p. 109

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Changing the active upper bound to \(u_j+\theta\) fixes \(x_j=u_j+\theta\) and changes the basic solution to \(x_B(\theta)=x_B^0-\theta B^{-1}A_j\). The upper-bound stability range is exactly the interval of \(\theta\) satisfying \(l_B\le x_B(\theta)\le u_B\) together with \(l_j\le u_j+\theta\). Since objective coefficients and the active-bound assignment are unchanged, reduced costs remain valid and the reference bounded-variable basis stays optimal throughout this interval.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An upper-bound change is allowable while the induced affine basic solution respects every bound and the modified upper bound remains above its lower bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Upper-Bound Ranges

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 7. Sensitivity and Parametric Analyses p. 109

children.title: Coupled Bound-Range Limits
children.top_down_role: Range restrictions arising from interactions between variable limits.

assumptions_latex: A bounded-variable LP has a fixed optimal basis \(B\), with nonbasic sets \(N_L\) and \(N_U\) fixed at lower and upper bounds.
Lower and upper bounds change by vectors \(d^l\) and \(d^u\), without changing nonbasic bound assignments.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(l_B+d_B^l\le x_B^0-B^{-1}(A_{N_L}d_{N_L}^l+A_{N_U}d_{N_U}^u)\le u_B+d_B^u\) and \(l+d^l\le u+d^u\).

notation.meaning: Nonbasic indices fixed at lower and upper bounds.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polyhedral limits for simultaneous bound changes under fixed bound statuses.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 7. Sensitivity and Parametric Analyses p. 109

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: With the nonbasic assignments fixed, simultaneous bound perturbations induce \(x_B(d^l,d^u)=x_B^0-B^{-1}(A_{N_L}d_{N_L}^l+A_{N_U}d_{N_U}^u)\). The coupled stability region consists exactly of perturbations satisfying \(l_B+d_B^l\le x_B(d^l,d^u)\le u_B+d_B^u\) and the consistency inequalities \(l+d^l\le u+d^u\). These inequalities couple otherwise separate allowable increases and decreases: independently computed one-bound ranges cannot generally be attained simultaneously. With unchanged costs and bound statuses, every point in this polyhedron preserves optimality of the reference basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Simultaneous bound changes must jointly preserve the affine basic solution, all perturbed bound orders, and the reference nonbasic bound assignments.
knowledge_statements.title: Coupled Bound-Range Limits

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 7. Sensitivity and Parametric Analyses p. 109

children.title: Objective-Coefficient Ranges
children.top_down_role: Local optimality ranges induced by changes in cost coefficients.

children.title: Nonbasic-Cost Optimality Ranges
children.top_down_role: Ranges controlled by nonbasic optimality margins.

assumptions_latex: The reference basis is optimal for \(\min\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\).
Only the objective coefficient \(c_j\) of one nonbasic variable \(j\in\mathcal N\) changes by \(\theta\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\theta\ge-r_j\), where \(r_j=c_j-A_j^TB^{-T}c_B\).

notation.meaning: Reference reduced cost of nonbasic variable j.
Change in the selected nonbasic objective coefficient.
Column of A associated with variable j.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-coefficient range for a nonbasic variable in minimization form.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 7. Sensitivity and Parametric Analyses p. 109

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(c_j\mapsto c_j+\theta\) for a single nonbasic index \(j\), then the dual vector \(y=B^{-T}c_B\) is unchanged. All other nonbasic reduced costs are unchanged, while \(r_j(\theta)=r_j+\theta\). Therefore the reference basis remains optimal exactly when \(r_j+	heta\ge0\), or equivalently \(\theta\ge-r_j\). In the standard-form minimization convention there is no finite upper restriction on this isolated coefficient increase.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For one nonbasic cost, the basis stays optimal exactly while that variable's shifted reduced cost remains nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonbasic-Cost Optimality Ranges

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 7. Sensitivity and Parametric Analyses p. 109

children.title: Basic-Cost Optimality Ranges
children.top_down_role: Ranges whose effects propagate through the dual-price structure.

assumptions_latex: The reference basis is optimal for \(\min\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\).
Only one basic coefficient \(c_{B,k}\) changes by \(\theta\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_N-\theta N^TB^{-T}e_k\ge0\).

notation.meaning: Reference vector of nonbasic reduced costs.
Coordinate vector selecting the changed basic cost.
Change in the selected basic objective coefficient.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-coefficient range for a basic variable in minimization form.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 7. Sensitivity and Parametric Analyses p. 109

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under \(c_B\mapsto c_B+\theta e_k\), the basis dual vector becomes \(y(\theta)=B^{-T}c_B+\theta B^{-T}e_k\). Consequently every nonbasic reduced cost changes according to \(r_N(\theta)=r_N-\theta N^TB^{-T}e_k\). The exact optimality range is the interval \(I_k=\{\theta:r_N-\theta N^TB^{-T}e_k\ge0\}\). Each nonbasic column may supply a lower bound, an upper bound, or no restriction on \(\theta\), depending on the sign of its coefficient in \(N^TB^{-T}e_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Changing a basic cost alters the dual vector and all reduced costs; their nonnegativity inequalities determine the exact allowable interval.
knowledge_statements.title: Basic-Cost Optimality Ranges

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 7. Sensitivity and Parametric Analyses p. 109

children.title: Reduced-Cost Dependence
children.top_down_role: Variation of opportunity-cost and nonbasic optimality information.

assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full row rank and is partitioned as \(A=[B\ N]\), where \(B\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}\) is nonsingular.
For the fixed right-hand side \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), the reference basic solution \(x_B=B^{-1}b\), \(x_N=0\), is primal feasible.
The objective changes from \(c\in\mathbb R^n\) to \(c+d\), where \(c=(c_B,c_N)\) and \(d=(d_B,d_N)\) are partitioned by the basic and nonbasic indices.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_N(c+d)=r_N(c)+d_N-N^TB^{-T}d_B\).

notation.meaning: Nonbasic reduced-cost vector at objective c.
Objective perturbation partitioned by basic and nonbasic indices.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine reduced-cost dependence for a fixed primal-feasible standard-form basis.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 7. Sensitivity and Parametric Analyses p. 109

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the fixed basis, the dual vector associated with objective \(c+d\) is \(y(c+d)=B^{-T}(c_B+d_B)\). Therefore the nonbasic reduced-cost vector satisfies \(r_N(c+d)=c_N+d_N-N^Ty(c+d)=r_N(c)+d_N-N^TB^{-T}d_B\). Thus reduced costs depend affinely on objective perturbations: nonbasic-cost changes act directly, whereas basic-cost changes propagate through the dual-price map \(B^{-T}\). Because the reference basic solution is primal feasible, the basis is optimal precisely when the resulting reduced-cost vector is componentwise nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a fixed primal-feasible basis, reduced costs vary affinely: nonbasic cost changes act directly, while basic cost changes propagate through the basis dual-price map; the basis is optimal exactly when the resulting reduced costs are nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.title: Reduced-Cost Dependence

children.title: Simultaneous-RHS Stability Regions
children.top_down_role: Joint RHS perturbations preserving reference-basis feasibility.

assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full row rank, and \(B=A_{[:,\mathcal B]}\) is a nonsingular reference basis.
The reference basis is optimal for \(\min\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\), with \(x_B^0=B^{-1}b\ge0\).
The right-hand side changes jointly by \(h\in\mathbb R^m\), while \(A\) and \(c\) remain fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal S_b=\{h\in\mathbb R^m:B^{-1}(b+h)\ge0\}\).

notation.meaning: RHS stability region of the reference basis.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact polyhedral region for simultaneous RHS changes and a fixed optimal basis.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 7. Sensitivity and Parametric Analyses p. 109

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a simultaneous perturbation \(b\mapsto b+h\), the basic variables determined by the reference basis are \(x_B(h)=B^{-1}(b+h)=x_B^0+B^{-1}h\), with \(x_N=0\). Hence the exact RHS stability region is the polyhedron \(\mathcal S_b=\{h:x_B^0+B^{-1}h\ge0\}\). Because objective coefficients are unchanged, dual feasibility of the reference optimal basis is unchanged; therefore every \(h\in\mathcal S_b\) preserves optimality. Its facets occur where one or more perturbed basic variables equal zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Joint RHS changes preserve the reference optimal basis exactly on the polyhedron where all induced basic-variable values remain nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.title: Simultaneous-RHS Stability Regions

children.title: Simultaneous-Cost Stability Regions
children.top_down_role: Joint objective perturbations preserving reference-basis optimality.

assumptions_latex: \(B\) is an optimal basis for \(\min\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\).
The objective changes jointly by \(d=(d_B,d_N)\), while \(A\) and \(b\) remain fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal S_c=\{d\in\mathbb R^n:r_N+d_N-N^TB^{-T}d_B\ge0\}\).

notation.meaning: Reference vector of nonbasic reduced costs.
Objective stability region of the reference basis.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact polyhedral region for simultaneous objective changes and a fixed basis.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 7. Sensitivity and Parametric Analyses p. 109

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a simultaneous objective perturbation \(c\mapsto c+d\), primal feasibility of the reference basic solution is unchanged. Its nonbasic reduced costs become \(r_N(d)=r_N+d_N-N^TB^{-T}d_B\). Accordingly, the exact cost-stability region is the polyhedron \(\mathcal S_c=\{d:r_N+d_N-N^TB^{-T}d_B\ge0\}\). Every perturbation in \(\mathcal S_c\) preserves optimality of the reference basis, while leaving this region through a strict facet makes at least one nonbasic reduced cost negative.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Joint cost changes preserve the reference basis on the polyhedron defined by nonnegativity of all affine perturbed reduced costs.
knowledge_statements.title: Simultaneous-Cost Stability Regions

children.title: 100% Rule Family
children.top_down_role: Classical sufficient-rule family for combining individual sensitivity information.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: On the 100% Rule of Sensitivity Analysis in Linear Programming
top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: 100% rule

knowledge_statements.title: 100% Rule Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient 100% rule for simultaneous RHS changes or simultaneous objective-coefficient changes, applied separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(d^0\in\mathbb R^q\), let \(e_i\) be the \(i\)-th coordinate vector, and let \(\mathcal S_B\subseteq\mathbb R^q\) be a convex fixed-basis stability region containing \(d^0\). For every perturbed coordinate \(i\), suppose \(d^0+D_i^+e_i\in\mathcal S_B\) and \(d^0-D_i^-e_i\in\mathcal S_B\), where \(D_i^+>0\) and \(D_i^->0\). A perturbation \(\Delta d\in\mathbb R^q\) obeying \(\sum_{i:\,\Delta d_i>0}\Delta d_i/D_i^++\sum_{i:\,\Delta d_i<0}(-\Delta d_i)/D_i^-\le1\) belongs to the sufficient 100% rule region, and \(d^0+\Delta d\in\mathcal S_B\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For one data family at a time, a fixed basis remains optimal if the sum of the simultaneous directional changes, each divided by its corresponding one-at-a-time allowable change, is at most 100%.
assumptions_latex: The nominal data vector satisfies \(d^0\in\mathcal S_B\subseteq\mathbb R^q\).
The fixed-basis stability region \(\mathcal S_B\) is convex.
For each perturbed coordinate \(i\), the directional endpoints satisfy \(d^0+D_i^+e_i\in\mathcal S_B\) and \(d^0-D_i^-e_i\in\mathcal S_B\), with \(D_i^+>0\) and \(D_i^->0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\sum_{i:\,\Delta d_i>0}\frac{\Delta d_i}{D_i^+}+\sum_{i:\,\Delta d_i<0}\frac{-\Delta d_i}{D_i^-}\le 1\quad\Longrightarrow\quad d^0+\Delta d\in\mathcal S_B.\]

notation.meaning: Nominal data vector and simultaneous perturbation.
The i-th coordinate vector in the data space.
Positive and negative one-at-a-time allowable changes.
Region in which the fixed basis B remains primal and dual feasible.

source_refs.locator: SIX: DUALITY AND SENSITIVITY ANALYSIS p. 259

children.title: Tolerance-Approach Families
children.top_down_role: Sensitivity regions based on bounded simultaneous data variation.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Linear Parametric Programming—A Brief Survey

assumptions_latex: A basis \(B\) is optimal for nominal data \(d^0\).
A nonnegative scaling vector \(s\) specifies absolute or relative perturbation widths.
The fixed-basis stability region \(\mathcal S_B\) is defined by primal and dual feasibility of \(B\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\tau_B^*=\sup\{\tau\ge0:[d^0-\tau s,d^0+\tau s]\subseteq\mathcal S_B\}.\]

notation.meaning: Nominal data vector and perturbation-width vector.
Maximum common tolerance for basis B.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Box-based absolute or relative tolerance analysis for bounded simultaneous LP-data variation.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 7. Sensitivity and Parametric Analyses p. 109

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(s\in\mathbb R_+^q\), the tolerance approach associates with basis \(B\) the largest scalar \(\tau_B^*\) such that every componentwise perturbation satisfying \(|\Delta d_i|\le\tau_B^*s_i\) leaves \(B\) optimal. Absolute tolerances use prescribed widths \(s_i\); relative tolerances may take \(s_i=|d_i^0|\), with a separately specified positive scale when \(d_i^0=0\). The tolerance family consists of the nested boxes \([d^0-\tau s,d^0+\tau s]\) contained in \(\mathcal S_B\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tolerance analysis finds the largest scaled box of simultaneous data changes entirely contained in the current basis-stability region.
knowledge_statements.title: Tolerance-Approach Families

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 7. Sensitivity and Parametric Analyses p. 109

children.title: Structural Model Changes
children.top_down_role: Postoptimal screening of added, removed, or modified rows and columns.

children.title: Candidate Variable-Column Interface
children.top_down_role: Postoptimal valuation and screening of candidate activities.

children.title: Candidate-Variable Valuation
children.top_down_role: Postoptimal valuation of a proposed decision variable.

knowledge_statements.title: Candidate-Variable Valuation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Basis-relative reduced-cost valuation for adding one nonnegative variable to a standard-form minimization LP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\) with an optimal basis matrix \(B\), basic costs \(c_B\), and multiplier \(y=B^{-T}c_B\). A candidate variable \(x_0\ge0\) with column \(a_0\) and cost \(c_0\) has basis-relative reduced cost \(\bar c_0=c_0-c_B^TB^{-1}a_0=c_0-y^Ta_0\). If \(\bar c_0\ge0\), adding the variable does not change the optimal value. If \(\bar c_0<0\), the candidate is eligible to enter and has objective rate \(\bar c_0\) along the associated simplex direction; strict improvement from the incumbent basis additionally requires a positive feasible step.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A candidate variable is valued at the incumbent basis by its reduced cost. A nonnegative reduced cost certifies no value improvement, while a negative reduced cost identifies an improving simplex direction only when a positive feasible step is available.
assumptions_latex: The standard-form minimization LP \(\min\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\) has an optimal basis matrix \(B\).
The candidate variable satisfies \(x_0\ge0\) and has objective coefficient \(c_0\) and column \(a_0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\bar c_0=c_0-y^Ta_0;\qquad \bar c_0\ge0\Longrightarrow z_{\mathrm{aug}}=z^*,\qquad \bar c_0<0\Longrightarrow x_0\text{ is eligible to enter}.\]

notation.meaning: Simplex multiplier associated with the incumbent basis.
Basis-relative reduced cost of the candidate variable.

source_refs.locator: 1. Sensitivity Analysis p. 109

source_witnesses.locator: 1. Sensitivity Analysis p. 109

children.title: Candidate-Column Screening
children.top_down_role: Postoptimal screening of a proposed matrix column.

assumptions_latex: The minimization LP \(\min\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\) has an optimal basis \(B\).
The candidate column \(a_0\) and its objective coefficient \(c_0\) are known.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[c_0-c_B^TB^{-1}a_0\ge0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\text{the candidate column may be screened out without changing the optimal value}.\]

notation.meaning: Current basis matrix and its basic costs.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual-feasibility screening certificate for a candidate column in standard-form minimization.

source_refs.locator: SIX: DUALITY AND SENSITIVITY ANALYSIS p. 259

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Compute \(y=B^{-T}c_B\) and the candidate reduced cost \(\bar c_0=c_0-y^Ta_0\). When \(\bar c_0\ge0\), the incumbent multiplier \(y\) satisfies the new dual inequality \(a_0^Ty\le c_0\). Thus the old primal optimum, extended by \(x_0=0\), and the old dual optimum remain feasible with equal objectives. The inequality \(\bar c_0\ge0\) is therefore a directly verifiable certificate that the candidate column cannot improve the minimization objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A candidate column is safely discarded when its reduced cost is nonnegative, because the incumbent dual solution remains feasible.
knowledge_statements.title: Candidate-Column Screening

source_witnesses.locator: SIX: DUALITY AND SENSITIVITY ANALYSIS p. 259

children.title: Variable–Column Representation Equivalence
children.top_down_role: Correspondence between activity-level and column-level interpretations.

assumptions_latex: The original model is \(\min\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\).
A new scalar decision variable \(x_0\ge0\) has coefficient \(c_0\) and constraint-incidence vector \(a_0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\min_{x,x_0}\{c^Tx+c_0x_0:Ax+a_0x_0=b,\ x\ge0,\ x_0\ge0\}=\min_{\tilde x}\{\tilde c^T\tilde x:\tilde A\tilde x=b,\ \tilde x\ge0\}.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact standard-form equivalence between adding a scalar variable and appending its matrix column.

source_refs.locator: SIX: DUALITY AND SENSITIVITY ANALYSIS p. 259

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Adding a nonnegative scalar variable \(x_0\) with objective coefficient \(c_0\) and incidence vector \(a_0\) is exactly the matrix operation of appending column \(a_0\) to \(A\) and component \(c_0\) to \(c\). Under the bijection \(\tilde x=(x,x_0)\), feasibility, objective values, and optimal solutions coincide. Consequently, candidate-variable valuation and candidate-column reduced-cost screening are two descriptions of the same augmented LP.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding a variable is exactly equivalent to appending its constraint column and objective coefficient to the standard-form LP.
knowledge_statements.title: Variable–Column Representation Equivalence

source_witnesses.locator: SIX: DUALITY AND SENSITIVITY ANALYSIS p. 259

children.title: Variable-Column Deletion Equivalence
children.top_down_role: Consequences of removing existing activities or columns.

children.title: Variable Deletion Effects
children.top_down_role: Optimality consequences of removing an existing decision variable.

knowledge_statements.title: Variable Deletion Effects
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasible-set and optimal-value effects of deleting one nonnegative variable from a minimization LP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=\{x\in\mathbb R_+^n:Ax=b\}\) and suppose \(z^*=\min_{x\in F}c^Tx\) is finite. Deleting variable \(x_j\) gives \(F_{-j}=F\cap\{x:x_j=0\}\). With the convention \(z_{-j}=+\infty\) when \(F_{-j}=\varnothing\), its optimal value satisfies \(z_{-j}\ge z^*\). Equality holds if and only if an original optimal solution has \(j\)-th component zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Deleting a variable restricts the feasible set and cannot improve a minimization value. It leaves the value unchanged exactly when an original optimum exists with that variable equal to zero.
assumptions_latex: The feasible set is \(F=\{x\in\mathbb R_+^n:Ax=b\}\), and \(z^*=\min_{x\in F}c^Tx\) is finite.
Variable \(x_j\) is deleted by imposing \(x_j=0\).
The deleted-model value is defined as \(z_{-j}=+\infty\) when its feasible set is empty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[F_{-j}=F\cap\{x:x_j=0\}\subseteq F,\qquad z_{-j}\ge z^*,\qquad z_{-j}=z^*\Longleftrightarrow\exists x^*\in\operatorname{argmin}_{x\in F}c^Tx\text{ with }x_j^*=0.\]

notation.meaning: Feasible set after deleting variable j.
Original and deleted-model optimal values under the extended-value convention.

source_refs.locator: SIX: DUALITY AND SENSITIVITY ANALYSIS p. 259

source_witnesses.locator: SIX: DUALITY AND SENSITIVITY ANALYSIS p. 259

children.title: Column Deletion Effects
children.top_down_role: Basis and model consequences of removing an existing matrix column.

knowledge_statements.title: Column Deletion Effects
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasible-set and optimal-value effects of deleting one column and its associated variable from a standard-form LP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In the standard-form LP \(\min\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\), removing column \(a_j\) and coefficient \(c_j\) produces \(\min\{c_{-j}^Tx_{-j}:A_{-j}x_{-j}=b,\ x_{-j}\ge0\}\). Its feasible solutions correspond to original feasible solutions with \(x_j=0\). Column deletion can therefore destroy feasibility or increase the minimum, and it leaves the value unchanged exactly when an original optimum has \(x_j=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Deleting a column removes its associated variable, restricts the original model to that variable being zero, and can make a minimization problem infeasible or increase its optimal value.
assumptions_latex: The LP is \(\min\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\).
Column \(a_j\) represents nonnegative variable \(x_j\) with cost coefficient \(c_j\).
The remaining columns, variables, and costs are denoted by \(A_{-j}\), \(x_{-j}\), and \(c_{-j}\).

notation.meaning: Variable vector with component j removed.
Cost vector with component j removed.

source_refs.locator: SIX: DUALITY AND SENSITIVITY ANALYSIS p. 259

source_witnesses.locator: SIX: DUALITY AND SENSITIVITY ANALYSIS p. 259

children.title: Deletion Representation Equivalence
children.top_down_role: Correspondence between variable removal and column removal.

assumptions_latex: The LP is in standard form \(\min\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\).
Index \(j\) identifies both scalar variable \(x_j\) and column \(a_j\) of \(A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[x_{-j}\longmapsto (x_1,\ldots,x_{j-1},0,x_{j+1},\ldots,x_n)\] is an objective-preserving bijection between the column-deleted feasible set and \(F\cap\{x:x_j=0\}\).

notation.meaning: Vectors and matrices after deleting index j.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective-preserving equivalence of variable deletion and deletion of its standard-form matrix column.

source_refs.locator: SIX: DUALITY AND SENSITIVITY ANALYSIS p. 259

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In standard form, variable \(x_j\), objective coefficient \(c_j\), and matrix column \(a_j\) constitute one model component. Deleting that variable is represented by deleting \(a_j\) and \(c_j\). The insertion map that restores \(x_j=0\) is a bijection from \(\{x_{-j}\ge0:A_{-j}x_{-j}=b\}\) onto \(F\cap\{x:x_j=0\}\), and it preserves objective values. Thus both deletion descriptions have identical feasibility, optimal-value, and optimizer effects.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Deleting a variable and deleting its matrix column plus cost coefficient are the same operation under zero-component insertion.
knowledge_statements.title: Deletion Representation Equivalence

source_witnesses.locator: SIX: DUALITY AND SENSITIVITY ANALYSIS p. 259

children.title: Candidate Constraint-Row Interface
children.top_down_role: Postoptimal screening of additional restrictions.

children.title: Candidate-Constraint Screening
children.top_down_role: Postoptimal assessment of a proposed model restriction.

assumptions_latex: The minimization LP has feasible set \(F\) and an optimal solution \(x^*\).
A candidate inequality is \(d^Tx\ge\beta\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[d^Tx^*\ge\beta\quad\Longrightarrow\quad x^*\in\operatorname{argmin}_{x\in F,\ d^Tx\ge\beta}c^Tx\ \text{ and }\ z_{\mathrm{aug}}=z^*.\]

notation.meaning: Original feasible set and incumbent optimizer.
Candidate constraint coefficients and right-hand side.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Incumbent-feasibility screening for adding one inequality to a minimization LP.

source_refs.locator: SIX: DUALITY AND SENSITIVITY ANALYSIS p. 259

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Adding \(d^Tx\ge\beta\) replaces \(F\) by \(F'=F\cap\{x:d^Tx\ge\beta\}\). If an incumbent optimizer \(x^*\) satisfies the candidate constraint, then \(x^*\in F'\). Because \(F'\subseteq F\), no point in \(F'\) has objective below \(c^Tx^*\), so \(x^*\) remains optimal and the value is unchanged. The check \(d^Tx^*\ge\beta\) is therefore a certificate for screening the candidate constraint against that optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A candidate inequality cannot change the optimum when the incumbent optimal solution already satisfies it.
knowledge_statements.title: Candidate-Constraint Screening

source_witnesses.locator: SIX: DUALITY AND SENSITIVITY ANALYSIS p. 259

children.title: Candidate-Row Screening
children.top_down_role: Postoptimal assessment of a proposed matrix row.

knowledge_statements.title: Candidate-Row Screening
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Slack-based screening of a candidate inequality row against a selected incumbent optimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a proposed row \(d^Tx-s=\beta\) with \(s\ge0\), evaluate a selected incumbent optimizer \(x^*\) and set \(s^*=d^Tx^*-\beta\). If \(s^*\ge0\), then \((x^*,s^*)\) is feasible and optimal for the row-augmented formulation. If \(s^*<0\), this certificate fails for the selected optimizer, but the sign alone does not determine whether another incumbent optimizer satisfies the row or whether the optimal value changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonnegative slack at a selected incumbent optimum certifies that the candidate row preserves that optimum. Negative slack only means this particular screening certificate fails.
assumptions_latex: The minimization LP has a selected incumbent optimal solution \(x^*\).
The proposed row is \(d^Tx-s=\beta\) with \(s\ge0\), representing \(d^Tx\ge\beta\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[s^*=d^Tx^*-\beta\ge0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad (x^*,s^*)\text{ is optimal for the row-augmented formulation}.\]

notation.meaning: Candidate row coefficients and right-hand side.
Slack variable for the candidate row.
Slack induced by the selected incumbent optimizer.

source_refs.locator: SIX: DUALITY AND SENSITIVITY ANALYSIS p. 259

source_witnesses.locator: SIX: DUALITY AND SENSITIVITY ANALYSIS p. 259

children.title: Constraint–Row Representation Equivalence
children.top_down_role: Correspondence between restriction-level and row-level interpretations.

assumptions_latex: The original feasible set is \(F=\{x:Ax\ge b,\ x\ge0\}\).
A candidate inequality has coefficients \(d\) and right-hand side \(\beta\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[F\cap\{x:d^Tx\ge\beta\}=\operatorname{proj}_x\{(x,s):Ax\ge b,\ d^Tx-s=\beta,\ x\ge0,\ s\ge0\}.\]

notation.meaning: Slack variable and projection onto x-space.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Slack-form equivalence between adding an inequality constraint and appending its matrix row.

source_refs.locator: 2.7 Representation of Polyhedral Sets p. 75

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Adding the inequality \(d^Tx\ge\beta\) is represented in equality form by appending the row \(d^Tx-s=\beta\) and introducing \(s\ge0\). For every feasible \(x\), the slack is uniquely determined as \(s=d^Tx-\beta\). Thus projection onto the original variables gives exactly the constraint-augmented feasible set, and objective values are unchanged when the slack has zero objective coefficient. Constraint screening and row screening are consequently equivalent under this slack representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding an inequality equals appending its slack-form row; projection removes the slack and recovers exactly the constrained feasible set.
