children.title: Enumeration Coverage Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Completeness limits associated with candidate-based regional construction.

knowledge_statements.title: Enumeration Coverage Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limits of structure enumeration as a complete parametric-regime description.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider finite-dimensional standard-form LPs \(P(\theta)=\min\{c(\theta)^\top x:Ax=b(\theta),\ x\geq0\}\) with \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) of rank \(m\). Exhaustive enumeration of all nonsingular bases covers every \(\theta\) at which \(P(\theta)\) has a finite optimum, because such an LP has an optimal basic feasible solution. Optimal-basis regions do not by themselves classify infeasible or unbounded parameters. Enumeration restricted to nondegenerate structures, strict-complementarity partitions, or facet-reachable full-dimensional regions may also omit lower-dimensional optimal strata or structures occurring only under degeneracy. Complete regime validation therefore additionally requires suitable feasibility, recession, or independently verified parameter-space coverage certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With full row rank, enumeration of every nonsingular basis covers all finite-optimum parameters, but it does not classify infeasible or unbounded parameters, and restricted enumeration can miss degenerate or lower-dimensional strata.
assumptions_latex: \(P(\theta)=\min\{c(\theta)^\top x:Ax=b(\theta),\ x\geq0\}\) is finite-dimensional for every \(\theta\in\Theta\).
\(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has rank \(m\).
Basis enumeration includes every \(B\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) with \(|B|=m\) and nonsingular \(A_B\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Theta_{\mathrm{fin}}\subseteq\bigcup_B\mathcal R_B\), while optimal-basis regions alone do not certify the infeasible or unbounded regimes.

notation.meaning: parameters for which the LP has a finite optimum

children.title: Geometric Subdivision Methods
children.top_down_role: Direct subdivision and management of parameter space.

knowledge_statements.title: Geometric Subdivision Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct polyhedral refinement of parameter space using regional status tests.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a polyhedral parameter domain \(\Theta\), an LP-status oracle, and a regional certificate generator. Initialize a cell collection with \(\Theta\). Select an uncertified cell \(C\), query parameters in \(C\), and attempt to construct inequalities defining a certified constant-status or constant-optimal-structure subset \(R\subseteq C\). Replace \(C\) by \(R\) and the polyhedral cells of \(C\setminus R\), discarding empty cells. Repeat until every remaining cell has a certificate or a declared unresolved status. Output the cells, their labels, and certificates; merge adjacent cells only when the merged cell admits the same certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly carve certified constant-status or constant-structure polyhedra from parameter space, subdividing unresolved remainders until all cells are labeled or flagged.
assumptions_latex: \(\Theta\) is polyhedral.
Generated regional certificates are valid throughout their asserted cells.
Polyhedral difference, emptiness, and merging operations are available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output cells have pairwise disjoint relative interiors and their union equals \(\Theta\), except for cells explicitly marked unresolved.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: This is a plausible algorithmic template, but no source or method-specific conditions establish termination, finite subdivision, or the asserted coverage and relative-interior disjointness invariants.

children.title: Parametric Regime Validation Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Finite, infeasible, and unbounded parameter regimes together with validation and structural-size issues.

children.title: Finite-Optimum Parameter Regions
children.top_down_role: Regions supporting feasible LPs with finite optima.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Optimum Parameter Regions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parameter set where a standard-form LP is feasible and bounded below.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(P(\theta)=\min\{c(\theta)^\top x:Ax=b(\theta),\ x\geq0\}\), the finite-optimum parameter region is \(\Theta_{\mathrm{fin}}=\{\theta\in\Theta:\exists x\geq0,\ Ax=b(\theta),\ \text{and }c(\theta)^\top d\geq0\text{ for every }d\geq0\text{ with }Ad=0\}\). Equivalently, it is the set of parameters for which the feasible set is nonempty and the objective is bounded below on that set. For each \(\theta\in\Theta_{\mathrm{fin}}\), the LP attains a finite minimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite-optimum parameters are exactly those with a feasible point and no feasible recession direction that strictly decreases the objective.
assumptions_latex: \(A\), \(b(\theta)\), and \(c(\theta)\) are finite-dimensional real LP data.
\(\Theta\) is the prescribed parameter domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\theta\in\Theta_{\mathrm{fin}}\Rightarrow\operatorname*{argmin}P(\theta)\neq\varnothing\) and \(-\infty<\min P(\theta)<+\infty\).

children.title: Infeasible Parameter Regions
children.top_down_role: Regions where parameterized constraints have no feasible solution.

knowledge_statements.title: Infeasible Parameter Regions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Farkas characterization of infeasible right-hand-side parameters.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(P(\theta)=\min\{c(\theta)^\top x:Ax=b(\theta),\ x\geq0\}\) with \(\theta\in\Theta\), define \(\Theta_{\mathrm{inf}}=\{\theta\in\Theta:\{x\in\mathbb R^n:x\geq0,\ Ax=b(\theta)\}=\varnothing\}\). By the equality-form Farkas alternative, \(\theta\in\Theta_{\mathrm{inf}}\) if and only if there exists \(y\in\mathbb R^m\) such that \(A^\top y\geq0\) and \(b(\theta)^\top y<0\). Such a vector \(y\) is an infeasibility certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A parameter is infeasible exactly when it admits a Farkas vector whose transpose product with every column of the constraint matrix is nonnegative but whose product with the right-hand side is negative.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\).
\(b(\theta)\in\mathbb R^m\) for every \(\theta\in\Theta\).
The primal variables satisfy \(x\in\mathbb R^n_+\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\theta\in\Theta_{\mathrm{inf}}\Longleftrightarrow\exists y\in\mathbb R^m:\ A^\top y\geq0,\ b(\theta)^\top y<0\).

children.title: Unbounded Parameter Regions
children.top_down_role: Regions where the parameterized objective lacks a finite optimum.

knowledge_statements.title: Unbounded Parameter Regions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parameters admitting a feasible point and a strictly improving recession direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(P(\theta)=\min\{c(\theta)^\top x:Ax=b(\theta),\ x\geq0\}\) with \(\theta\in\Theta\), define \(\Theta_{\mathrm{unb}}\) as the set of parameters for which \(P(\theta)\) is feasible and unbounded below. Equivalently, \(\theta\in\Theta_{\mathrm{unb}}\) if and only if there exist \(x,d\in\mathbb R^n\) satisfying \(x\geq0\), \(Ax=b(\theta)\), \(d\geq0\), \(Ad=0\), and \(c(\theta)^\top d<0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An unbounded parameter is exactly one having a feasible point and a nonnegative null-space direction that strictly decreases the objective.
assumptions_latex: \(P(\theta)\) is a finite-dimensional standard-form minimization LP for every \(\theta\in\Theta\).
\(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b(\theta)\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(c(\theta)\in\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\theta\in\Theta_{\mathrm{unb}}\Longleftrightarrow\exists x,d\in\mathbb R^n:\ x\geq0,\ Ax=b(\theta),\ d\geq0,\ Ad=0,\ c(\theta)^\top d<0\).

children.title: Regional Status Certificate System
children.top_down_role: Primal-dual and alternative-system validation of parameter-region status.

children.title: Regional Optimality Certificates
children.top_down_role: Validation of finite-optimum status over a parameter region.

knowledge_statements.title: Regional Optimality Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise primal-dual certificate mappings valid throughout one parameter region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A regional optimality certificate on \(R\subseteq\Theta\) consists of mappings \(x_R:R\to\mathbb{R}^n\), \(y_R:R\to\mathbb{R}^m\), and \(s_R:R\to\mathbb{R}^n\) such that, for every \(\theta\in R\), \[A(\theta)x_R(\theta)=b(\theta),\quad x_R(\theta)\geq0,\quad A(\theta)^\top y_R(\theta)+s_R(\theta)=c(\theta),\quad s_R(\theta)\geq0,\] and \[x_R(\theta)^\top s_R(\theta)=0.\] These primal-feasibility, dual-feasibility, and complementary-slackness conditions certify that \(x_R(\theta)\) is optimal with finite optimal value for every \(\theta\in R\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Regional primal and dual mappings certify finite optimality at every parameter where primal feasibility, dual feasibility, and complementary slackness hold.
assumptions_latex: The parameter set is \(\Theta\subseteq\mathbb{R}^p\).
For every \(\theta\in\Theta\), \(A(\theta)\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(b(\theta)\in\mathbb{R}^m\), and \(c(\theta)\in\mathbb{R}^n\).
The regional primal problem is \(\min\{c(\theta)^\top x:A(\theta)x=b(\theta),\ x\geq0\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every \(\theta\in R\) has a finite optimum certified by \((x_R(\theta),y_R(\theta),s_R(\theta))\).

notation.meaning: Regional primal and dual certificate mappings

children.title: Regional Infeasibility Certificates

knowledge_statements.title: Regional Infeasibility Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Farkas certificates for equality-form, nonnegative-variable feasibility systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A regional infeasibility certificate on \(R\subseteq\Theta\) is a mapping \(y_R:R\to\mathbb{R}^m\) satisfying, for every \(\theta\in R\), \[A(\theta)^\top y_R(\theta)\geq0\quad\text{and}\quad b(\theta)^\top y_R(\theta)<0.\] These relations certify that \(A(\theta)x=b(\theta)\), \(x\geq0\), is infeasible for every \(\theta\in R\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A regional Farkas multiplier certifies infeasibility wherever its transformed coefficients are nonnegative and its right-hand-side pairing is strictly negative.
assumptions_latex: The parameter set is \(\Theta\subseteq\mathbb{R}^p\).
For every \(\theta\in\Theta\), \(A(\theta)\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) and \(b(\theta)\in\mathbb{R}^m\).
The proposed certificate mapping is defined on \(R\subseteq\Theta\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The system \(A(\theta)x=b(\theta),\ x\geq0\) is infeasible for every \(\theta\in R\).

children.title: Regional Unboundedness Certificates
children.top_down_role: Validation of unbounded status over a parameter region.

knowledge_statements.title: Regional Unboundedness Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal feasible-point and improving recession-direction certificates for minimization-form LPs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A regional unboundedness certificate on \(R\subseteq\Theta\) consists of mappings \(x_R,d_R:R\to\mathbb{R}^n\) such that, for every \(\theta\in R\), \[A(\theta)x_R(\theta)=b(\theta),\quad x_R(\theta)\geq0,\] and \[A(\theta)d_R(\theta)=0,\quad d_R(\theta)\geq0,\quad c(\theta)^\top d_R(\theta)<0.\] These conditions certify that the objective infimum is \(-\infty\) for every \(\theta\in R\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible point and a nonnegative feasible direction with strictly negative cost certify unboundedness throughout a parameter region.
assumptions_latex: The parameter set is \(\Theta\subseteq\mathbb{R}^p\).
For every \(\theta\in\Theta\), \(A(\theta)\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(b(\theta)\in\mathbb{R}^m\), and \(c(\theta)\in\mathbb{R}^n\).
The regional problem is \(\min\{c(\theta)^\top x:A(\theta)x=b(\theta),\ x\geq0\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The objective infimum equals \(-\infty\) for every \(\theta\in R\).

children.title: Certificate Validity Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Parameter limits across which a regional status certificate ceases to apply.

assumptions_latex: A regional certificate is expressed by finitely many continuous residual functions \(g_i(\theta)\geq0\), \(h_j(\theta)=0\), and strict margins \(q_k(\theta)>0\).
Its validity set is restricted to a parameter domain \(\Theta\subseteq\mathbb{R}^p\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Validity can change only on \(\partial\Theta\) or where an active certificate margin reaches zero or an equality residual ceases to vanish.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary characterization for certificates encoded by continuous equality, weak-inequality, and strict-inequality residuals.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 7. Sensitivity and Parametric Analyses p. 109

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The validity set of the certificate is \[V=\{\theta\in\Theta:g_i(\theta)\geq0\ \forall i,\ h_j(\theta)=0\ \forall j,\ q_k(\theta)>0\ \forall k\}.\] At any \(\theta\in\operatorname{int}\Theta\) where all strict margins remain positive, all required weak inequalities hold with positive margin, and all equality identities persist locally, certificate validity is locally unchanged. Hence a validity boundary is contained in \[\partial\Theta\ \cup\ \bigcup_i\{\theta:g_i(\theta)=0\}\ \cup\ \bigcup_k\{\theta:q_k(\theta)=0\}\ \cup\ \bigcup_j\partial\{\theta:h_j(\theta)=0\}.\] Crossing such a set may invalidate the certificate, but equality alone need not change status under degeneracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Certificate status can change only at the parameter-domain boundary or where a required residual loses its defining sign or equality property.
knowledge_statements.title: Certificate Validity Boundaries

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 7. Sensitivity and Parametric Analyses p. 109

children.title: Parametric Output Complexity
children.top_down_role: Growth in scalar path segments and multiparametric critical regions.

children.title: Scalar Breakpoint Complexity
children.top_down_role: Growth of breakpoints or path segments along scalar parameter trajectories.

assumptions_latex: The scalar parameter ranges over an interval \(I\subseteq\mathbb{R}\).
The constraint matrix is fixed, the right-hand side and objective are affine in the parameter, and each reported regime is supported by a primal basis.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The number of breakpoints is at most \(\binom{m}{n}-1\), while worst-case families can have \(2^{\Omega(n)}\) breakpoints.

notation.meaning: Number of constraints and rank-sized basis columns

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Combinatorial worst-case bound for one-parameter, fixed-matrix LP basis regimes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\) be the number of nonempty maximal intervals on which one primal basis supplies a valid optimal solution formula, and let \(B=K-1\) count their interior breakpoints. If \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times m}\) has rank \(n\), then at most \(\binom{m}{n}\) column bases exist, so \[B\leq K-1\leq\binom{m}{n}-1.\] This combinatorial bound is exponential when both dimensions vary. Moreover, there are one-parameter LP families of encoding size polynomial in \(n\) whose optimal basis sequence contains \(2^{\Omega(n)}\) distinct regimes; thus polynomial breakpoint complexity cannot be guaranteed from input size alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A scalar parametric LP has at most one regime per basis, yet the number of breakpoints can grow exponentially with dimension.
knowledge_statements.title: Scalar Breakpoint Complexity

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound kind fits, and the combinatorial upper bound is plausible under the stated basis convention, but no source supports the exponential lower-bound family or confirms the exact regime-count convention.

children.title: Critical-Region Complexity
children.top_down_role: Growth of critical regions in multiparametric LP descriptions.

assumptions_latex: The parameter lies in a polyhedron \(\Theta\subseteq\mathbb{R}^p\).
The LP has a fixed rank-\(n\) constraint matrix with \(m\) columns and affine parameter dependence in its objective or right-hand side.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The number \(K\) of full-dimensional basis regions satisfies \(K\leq\binom{m}{n}\), and exponential growth is possible.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Basis-indexed full-dimensional critical regions in multiparametric linear programming.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each nonsingular basis \(B\), primal and dual feasibility of its affine solution formula define a polyhedral parameter set \(R_B\subseteq\Theta\). After discarding empty sets and identifying coincident full-dimensional cells, the number \(K\) of basis-indexed critical regions obeys \[K\leq\#\{B:B\text{ is a nonsingular basis}\}\leq\binom{m}{n}.\] Degeneracy may make several bases represent the same region, so it cannot increase the number beyond the number of bases under this convention. Since \(\binom{m}{n}\) can be exponential in the variable input dimensions and scalar parametric families already attain exponentially many regimes, no general polynomial input-size bound on \(K\) exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each full-dimensional critical region is supported by a basis, giving a combinatorial upper bound and permitting exponentially many regions in the worst case.
knowledge_statements.title: Critical-Region Complexity

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The claim depends on a precise definition of basis-indexed critical regions and treatment of degeneracy and coincident cells. No cited source supports those conventions or the worst-case exponential conclusion.

children.title: Output-Size Growth Regimes
children.top_down_role: Structural regimes governing the size of explicit parametric outputs.

assumptions_latex: An explicit parametric solution reports every maximal status region and its certificate or affine solution description.
The input encoding length is \(L\), and the explicit output contains \(K\) regions with total encoding length \(S\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Explicit enumeration requires \(\Omega(S)\) time, and \(S\) may be \(2^{\Omega(L)}\) even though particular fixed-dimensional families have polynomial growth.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Input-size versus explicit-output-size regimes for complete parametric LP descriptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Any algorithm producing the explicit regional description must write \(S\) symbols, and therefore has running time \(\Omega(S)\) in a standard bit model. Because \(S\geq K\), families with \(K=2^{\Omega(L)}\) force exponential enumeration time independently of the LP solver used. Conversely, when the number of admissible bases is polynomial in \(L\), each region has a polynomial-length rational description, and duplicate removal is polynomially controlled, one has \(S=\operatorname{poly}(L)\). Thus the natural growth regimes are output-polynomial, output-exponential, and representation-dominated regimes where regional descriptions themselves control \(S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Explicit enumeration costs at least the output length; polynomial and exponential regimes depend on both region count and regional-description size.
knowledge_statements.title: Output-Size Growth Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The output-length lower bound is standard, but the asserted \(K=2^{\Omega(L)}\) does not follow merely from a family exponential in dimension with polynomial encoding size. The growth regimes and polynomial-output converse also require precise sourced hypotheses.

children.title: Output-Sensitive Region Enumeration
children.top_down_role: Enumeration complexity measured against the explicit regional output.

assumptions_latex: The full-dimensional critical regions form a finite, connected polyhedral subdivision of the parameter domain.
Each facet has at most one unexplored adjacent region, and LP feasibility, redundancy, and adjacency tests run in polynomial time in the rational input length.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The traversal outputs every critical region once using \(O(K\operatorname{poly}(L,m,n,p))\) time under the stated oracle and nondegeneracy assumptions.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional facet-adjacency traversal with complexity measured against the explicit regional output.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input the rational parametric LP and one parameter \(\theta_0\) in a full-dimensional critical region. Compute that region, initialize \(Q\) with its canonical signature, and set \(H=\varnothing\). While \(Q\neq\varnothing\), remove a signature \(R\); if \(R\notin H\), output its irredundant inequalities and certificate, insert \(R\) into \(H\), and test a point across each facet to compute any adjacent region \(R'\), inserting unseen signatures into \(Q\). Stop when \(Q=\varnothing\). Under the assumptions, every region is reached and processed once, giving total time \[O\!\left(K\operatorname{poly}(L,m,n,p)\right)\] and polynomial delay between consecutive outputs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Traverse the facet-adjacency graph, canonically deduplicate regions, and output each once; under explicit assumptions, runtime is polynomial per reported region.

knowledge_statements.title: Resource-Value Interpretation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global supergradient and local marginal-value interpretation for the concave LP value function on its effective domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\) be the set of right-hand sides \(b'\) for which \(v(b')=\max\{c^\top x:Ax\leq b',\ x\geq0\}\) has a finite optimum. If \(y^*\) is dual optimal at \(b\in D\), then, for every \(b'\in D\), \[v(b')\leq v(b)+(y^*)^\top(b'-b).\] Thus \(y^*\) is a supergradient of the concave value function \(v\) at \(b\). If \(b\in\operatorname{int}D\) and \(v\) is differentiable at \(b\), then \[\nabla v(b)=y^*.\] At a nondifferentiable point, distinct dual optimizers may provide distinct supporting marginal valuations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An optimal dual vector supports the concave resource-value function from above and equals its marginal-value gradient at an interior differentiable point.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The vector \(y^*\) is a supergradient of \(v\) at \(b\), and \(\nabla v(b)=y^*\) when \(b\in\operatorname{int}D\) and \(v\) is differentiable at \(b\).

knowledge_statements.title: Reduced-Cost Interpretation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Maximization convention: reduced costs are nonpositive at a primal-dual optimum and value activities net of resource prices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the primal-dual pair \(\max\{c^\top x:Ax\leq b,\ x\geq0\}\) and \(\min\{b^\top y:A^\top y\geq c,\ y\geq0\}\), the reduced cost of activity \(j\) at dual prices \(y^*\) is \[r_j=c_j-a_j^\top y^*.\] At a primal-dual optimum \((x^*,y^*)\), dual feasibility gives \(r_j\leq0\), and complementary slackness gives \(x_j^*r_j=0\). For an inactive activity with \(x_j^*=0\), \(r_j\) is its direct return minus the dual-price value of the resources it consumes. A strictly negative reduced cost indicates unfavorable net return at the current prices; a zero reduced cost removes this price-based penalty but does not by itself guarantee a distinct feasible optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reduced cost is an activity's return minus the value of the resources it consumes; at an optimum it is nonpositive, and zero reduced cost alone does not guarantee another optimum.
assumptions_latex: The primal-dual pair is \(\max\{c^\top x:Ax\leq b,\ x\geq0\}\) and \(\min\{b^\top y:A^\top y\geq c,\ y\geq0\}\).
The pair \((x^*,y^*)\) is primal-dual optimal.
The vector \(a_j\) is column \(j\) of \(A\), and \(c_j\) is the objective coefficient of activity \(j\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every activity \(j\), \(r_j=c_j-a_j^\top y^*\leq0\) and \(x_j^*r_j=0\); for an inactive activity, \(r_j\) measures net return after charging resources at dual prices.

knowledge_statements.title: Opportunity-Value Interpretation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Opportunity value for an inactive variable in a standard-form maximization LP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider 
\[v=\max\{c^\top x:Ax\le b,\ x\ge0\},\qquad \min\{b^\top y:A^\top y\ge c,\ y\ge0\}.\]
For primal-dual optimal solutions \(x^*\) and \(y^*\), define \(r_j=c_j-a_j^\top y^*\le0\). If \(x_j^*=0\), then \(-r_j=a_j^\top y^*-c_j\) is the opportunity loss per marginal unit of activity \(j\): its resource value at prices \(y^*\) exceeds its objective return by \(-r_j\). Equivalently, with prices and other data fixed, the coefficient \(c_j\) must increase by at least \(-r_j\) before activity \(j\) can have zero reduced cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an inactive activity, minus its reduced cost is the amount by which its unit resource value exceeds its return, or the coefficient improvement needed to reach break-even.
assumptions_latex: \(x^*\) and \(y^*\) are optimal and strong duality holds.
Activity \(j\) is at its lower bound: \(x_j^*=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(-r_j=a_j^\top y^*-c_j\ge0\) is the activity's marginal opportunity loss.

knowledge_statements.title: Slack Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classification of a resource constraint by positive primal slack.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In the maximization problem \(\max\{c^\top x:Ax\le b,\ x\ge0\}\), define the slack of constraint \(i\) at an optimal solution \(x^*\) by \(s_i=b_i-a_i^\top x^*\). Constraint \(i\) is in a slack regime at \(x^*\) exactly when \(s_i>0\). For every dual optimum \(y^*\) complementary to \(x^*\), complementary slackness gives \(y_i^*s_i=0\), hence \(y_i^*=0\). Therefore a locally unchanged optimal basis assigns zero basis-local marginal value to additional units of that resource while the slack remains positive.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constraint is in a slack regime when unused capacity is positive; complementary optimal prices then assign that constraint zero marginal value.
assumptions_latex: \(x^*\) is primal optimal.
\(y^*\) is a complementary dual optimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s_i>0\) characterizes the slack regime and implies \(y_i^*=0\).

notation.meaning: slack b_i-a_i^T x* of constraint i

children.title: Scarcity Regimes

knowledge_statements.title: Scarcity Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive-price regime for a resource constraint in a maximization LP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\max\{c^\top x:Ax\le b,\ x\ge0\}\) with an optimal primal-dual pair \((x^*,y^*)\), constraint \(i\) is in a scarcity regime relative to the selected price system when \(y_i^*>0\). Complementary slackness then gives \(b_i-a_i^\top x^*=0\), so the resource is fully used. If an optimal basis \(B\) induces the selected price vector through \((y^*)^\top=c_B^\top B^{-1}\) and remains optimal under \(b_i\mapsto b_i+\delta\), then the optimal value changes by \(y_i^*\delta\). Binding alone does not characterize scarcity because a binding constraint may have zero selected price.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A resource is scarce under a selected optimal price system when its dual price is positive; it is then binding, and when that price is induced by a persisting optimal basis it gives the basis-local marginal value.
assumptions_latex: \((x^*,y^*)\) is an optimal primal-dual pair.
For the value-change formula, \(B\) is an optimal basis inducing \(y^*\) and remains optimal after the stated perturbation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y_i^*>0\) implies \(b_i-a_i^\top x^*=0\); under the basis-persistence assumptions, the value change is \(y_i^*\delta\).

children.title: Binding-Regime Transitions

knowledge_statements.title: Binding-Regime Transitions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Basis-local transition between slack and binding status under RHS variation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix a nonsingular optimal basis \(B\) after introducing slack variables, and perturb the right-hand side along \(b(t)=b+td\). While \(B\) remains optimal, its basic solution satisfies
\[x_B(t)=B^{-1}b+tB^{-1}d.\]
Consequently, every constraint slack is affine in \(t\). A constraint changes from slack to binding within this basis-local description at a parameter value where its slack reaches zero. The fixed basis remains primal feasible exactly for
\[T_B=\{t:B^{-1}(b+td)\ge0\}.\]
At a boundary of \(T_B\), some basic variable reaches zero; if that variable is the relevant slack and continuation would make it negative, the same basis cannot describe the constraint beyond the transition. A pivot or another optimal basis may then be required, and the associated shadow-price vector may change.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under a fixed optimal basis, constraint slacks vary affinely with the RHS parameter. A slack-to-binding transition occurs when the relevant slack reaches zero; general basis breakpoints can also arise when other basic variables reach zero.
assumptions_latex: \(B\) is nonsingular and optimal at \(t=0\).
Only the right-hand side varies as \(b+td\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A basis-local slack-to-binding transition for constraint \(i\) occurs where its affine slack satisfies \(s_i(t)=0\), within a boundary of \(T_B=\{t:B^{-1}(b+td)\ge0\}\).

notation.meaning: current basis matrix including slack columns
parameter set on which the fixed basis is primal feasible

children.title: Alternative Optimal Price Systems
children.top_down_role: Economic interpretation of nonunique optimal dual solutions.

knowledge_statements.title: Alternative Optimal Price Systems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonunique dual optima as alternative resource-price systems and directional valuations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a finite optimal value
\[v(b)=\max\{c^\top x:Ax\le b,\ x\ge0\},\]
define the optimal price set
\[Y^*(b)=\operatorname*{argmin}\{b^\top y:A^\top y\ge c,\ y\ge0\}.\]
This set is a convex polyhedron and may contain multiple price vectors even when \(v(b)\) is unique. Every \(y\in Y^*(b)\) supports the value function through \(v(b+d)\le v(b)+y^\top d\) whenever the perturbed problem is feasible. If \(v\) is finite in a neighborhood of \(b\), its one-sided directional derivative satisfies
\[v'(b;d)=\min_{y\in Y^*(b)}y^\top d.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonunique dual optima are alternative price systems. Each supports the value function, while a perturbation direction selects the smallest price pairing as its directional derivative.
assumptions_latex: The primal and dual attain the common finite value \(v(b)\).
For the derivative formula, \(v\) is finite near \(b\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Y^*(b)\) is the set of valid supporting price systems and \(v'(b;d)=\min_{y\in Y^*(b)}y^\top d\).

notation.meaning: optimal primal value as a function of resources
set of optimal dual price vectors

children.title: Price-Sign Conventions

knowledge_statements.title: Price-Sign Conventions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Shadow-price signs under equivalent multiplier and value-derivative conventions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For
\[v(b)=\max\{c^\top x:Ax\le b,\ x\ge0\},\]
the nonnegative dual convention uses \(y\ge0\), dual objective \(b^\top y\), and Lagrangian \(L(x,y)=c^\top x+y^\top(b-Ax)\). If instead constraints are written as \(Ax-b\le0\) and the Lagrangian is written \(c^\top x-\lambda^\top(Ax-b)\), then \(\lambda=y\ge0\). A convention using \(L=c^\top x+\mu^\top(Ax-b)\) requires \(\mu=-y\le0\). Thus the economic shadow price is \(y=-\mu\), and, where differentiable, \(\partial v/\partial b_i=y_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multiplier signs depend on how constraints enter the Lagrangian; translating them restores the same nonnegative economic shadow price for an upper resource constraint.
assumptions_latex: The displayed maximization LP has a finite attained optimum.
The value function is differentiable when an ordinary derivative is asserted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Equivalent conventions satisfy \(y=\lambda=-\mu\), with economic price \(y_i=\partial v/\partial b_i\) where differentiable.

notation.meaning: multipliers under two Lagrangian sign conventions

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Orientation Conventions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Translation of dual multipliers when an inequality row is reversed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A constraint row \(a_i^\top x\le b_i\) may be represented equivalently as \((-a_i)^\top x\ge-b_i\). If \(y_i\ge0\) is its multiplier under the upper-bound resource convention, then the signed multiplier attached to the reversed row is \(\widehat y_i=-y_i\le0\). The stationarity contribution is invariant because
\[y_i a_i=\widehat y_i(-a_i),\]
and the dual objective contribution is invariant because \(b_i y_i=(-b_i)\widehat y_i\). Consequently, constraint reversal changes the reported multiplier's sign but not the dual bound, reduced costs, or economic valuation after translation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reversing an inequality row reverses its signed multiplier. After this sign change, stationarity, dual value, reduced costs, and economic meaning remain unchanged.
assumptions_latex: The row is multiplied by \(-1\) without changing its feasible set.
Multiplier signs follow the stated upper- and lower-inequality conventions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat y_i=-y_i\) is the orientation translation preserving all dual contributions.

notation.meaning: multiplier for the original less-than-or-equal row

knowledge_statements.title: Objective-Orientation Conventions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Translation of prices and reduced costs between maximization and negated minimization objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Replacing the maximization objective \(c^\top x\) by the equivalent minimization objective \((-c)^\top x\) negates the optimal value and all signed objective sensitivities. If \(r_j^{\max}=c_j-a_j^\top y\) denotes the maximization reduced cost and the minimization formulation uses consistently negated dual multipliers \(z=-y\), then
\[r_j^{\min}=(-c_j)-a_j^\top z=-r_j^{\max}.\]
Likewise, if \(v_{\min}(b)=-v_{\max}(b)\), then every corresponding signed RHS sensitivity satisfies \(g_{
\min}=-g_{\max}\). Economic resource values remain unchanged only after the reporting convention is translated back to the original objective orientation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Negating the objective converts maximization to minimization and negates values, reduced costs, and signed sensitivities; translation recovers the original economic interpretation.
assumptions_latex: The feasible region is unchanged.
Dual multipliers and reduced costs are defined consistently with each objective orientation.

children.title: Solver-Convention Translation
children.top_down_role: Translation between solver output conventions and model-level economic meaning.

knowledge_statements.title: Solver-Convention Translation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normalization procedure for solver-reported prices, duals, and reduced costs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Input a solver row written as \(\sigma_i a_i^\top x\le \sigma_i b_i\), an objective multiplier \(\tau\in\{1,-1\}\), and reported row multiplier \(m_i\) and reduced cost \(q_j\), where \(\sigma_i\in\{1,-1\}\) records row reversal and \(\tau=-1\) records objective negation relative to the reference maximization model. First map the row to its reference orientation; then map the objective to maximization. Under a solver convention whose reported signed quantities transform covariantly, set
\[y_i=\tau\sigma_i m_i,\qquad r_j=\tau q_j.\]
Finally verify dual feasibility, reduced-cost signs, complementary slackness, and equality of primal and dual objectives. Reject the translation if any check fails.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Translate solver sensitivities by undoing row reversal and objective negation, then validate signs and values through dual feasibility, complementarity, and strong duality.
assumptions_latex: Solver documentation identifies the meanings of \(m_i\) and \(q_j\).
Only row reversal and objective negation separate solver and reference conventions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The accepted reference quantities are \(y_i=\tau\sigma_i m_i\) and \(r_j=\tau q_j\), subject to the validation checks.

notation.meaning: solver-reported row multiplier and reduced cost

children.title: RHS Ranging Reports

knowledge_statements.title: RHS Ranging Reports
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Basis-preserving intervals and shadow values for one-at-a-time RHS perturbations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix an optimal basis \(B\) and vary only right-hand side component \(b_i\) by \(\delta\). The reported allowable interval is the maximal interval containing zero on which
\[x_B(\delta)=B^{-1}b+\delta B^{-1}e_i\ge0.\]
Because reduced costs do not depend on \(b\), dual feasibility of the fixed basis is unchanged. Throughout this interval the basis remains optimal and
\[v(b+\delta e_i)=v(b)+y_i\delta,\qquad y^\top=c_B^\top B^{-1}.\]
Endpoints occur when a basic variable reaches a bound. The report is basis-local: degeneracy may permit another optimal basis or a wider unchanged-value region beyond a reported endpoint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An RHS range is the one-at-a-time interval preserving primal feasibility of the reported optimal basis; within it, the objective changes linearly at the reported shadow price.
assumptions_latex: \(B\) is an optimal nonsingular basis.
Only \(b_i\) varies and all other data remain fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The basis-preserving range is \(\{\delta:B^{-1}b+\delta B^{-1}e_i\ge0\}\), with value change \(y_i\delta\).

notation.meaning: ith coordinate vector in RHS space
basis dual vector satisfying y^T=c_B^T B^{-1}

children.title: Objective-Coefficient Ranging Reports

knowledge_statements.title: Objective-Coefficient Ranging Reports
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Basis-preserving intervals for one-at-a-time objective-coefficient perturbations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the standard-form maximization problem \(\max\{c^\top x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\), fix a primal- and dual-feasible basis \(B\). If variable \(j\) is nonbasic and only its coefficient varies from \(c_j\) to \(c_j+\delta\), the basic solution is unchanged and
\[r_j(\delta)=c_j+\delta-c_B^\top B^{-1}a_j=r_j+\delta.\]
The fixed basis remains optimal exactly while \(r_j+\delta\le0\), together with the unchanged reduced-cost inequalities for all other nonbasic variables. If a basic coefficient varies instead, all nonbasic reduced costs vary affinely, and their simultaneous optimal-sign inequalities determine the allowable interval. Reported endpoints are basis-local and, under degeneracy, need not delimit persistence of the same optimal solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An objective-coefficient range is the interval over which all reduced costs retain their optimal signs for the selected basis; the primal basic solution then stays unchanged.
assumptions_latex: \(B\) is a primal- and dual-feasible optimal basis.
Only one objective coefficient varies.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The allowable coefficient interval is the maximal interval containing zero on which every nonbasic reduced-cost inequality for the fixed basis remains satisfied.

children.top_down_role: Reported ranges for lower and upper variable bounds.

children.top_down_role: Solver-reported dual values or reduced-cost quantities.

assumptions_latex: The LP \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\) has an optimal primal-dual pair.
The displayed dual convention is \(A^{\mathsf T}y\le c\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(v(b)=\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\), a marginal report lists an optimal dual vector \(y\) satisfying \(A^{\mathsf T}y\le c\) and \(b^{\mathsf T}y=v(b)\). If the reported optimal basis remains optimal for \(b+t e_i\) throughout an interval containing \(0\), then \(v(b+t e_i)=v(b)+t y_i\) on that interval. Thus \(y_i\) is the reported local objective change per unit right-hand-side change, under the stated minimization and dual-sign convention.

children.title: Slack Reports

assumptions_latex: Rows are written as \(a_i^{\mathsf T}x\le b_i\).
The reported point \(x\) is primal feasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each reported slack is \(s_i=b_i-a_i^{\mathsf T}x\ge0\), and zero slack identifies an active row.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a row \(a_i^{\mathsf T}x\le b_i\), its slack report contains \(s_i=b_i-a_i^{\mathsf T}x\). Primal feasibility gives \(s_i\ge0\); the row is active exactly when \(s_i=0\). For a lower-bound row \(a_i^{\mathsf T}x\ge b_i\), the nonnegative slack is instead \(a_i^{\mathsf T}x-b_i\). For an equality row the residual must be zero, so no nonnegative one-sided slack has an independent meaning. Solver reports must therefore be interpreted together with each row's sense.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Slack is the signed distance from row activity to its permitted bound, using the row's inequality sense.

The solver reports a primal feasible point \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The activity report gives \(q_i=a_i^{\mathsf T}x\), from which lower and upper slacks are obtained by subtraction.

When the corresponding bound is finite, the lower and upper slacks are \(q_i-L_i\) and \(U_i-q_i\), respectively, and primal feasibility requires both to be nonnegative. An activity equals a finite row bound exactly when that side is active. Activities are primal quantities and do not, by themselves, measure objective sensitivity.

The report gives a primal-dual optimal pair \((x,y)\) with \(y\ge0\).

A mutually consistent optimal report satisfies \(x,s,y,r\ge0\), \(Ax+s=b\), \(A^{\mathsf T}y-r=c\), \(y_i s_i=0\) for every row, \(x_j r_j=0\) for every variable, and \(c^{\mathsf T}x=b^{\mathsf T}y\). A particular basis \(B\) is optimal at \(\theta_0\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If a selected basis \(B\) remains primal and dual feasible as \(\theta\) varies, then it remains an optimality certificate and its basis-induced solution remains an optimizer. That solution may vary with \(\theta\), so preservation of \(B\) does not imply preservation of a fixed optimizer vector. Conversely, under degeneracy, distinct bases can represent the same optimizer, and a selected basis can be replaced by another optimal basis without changing the represented optimizer or the optimizer set \(X^\ast(\theta)\). Thus a basis-validity interval is not, without additional uniqueness and nondegeneracy assumptions, an interval on which either a fixed optimizer or the complete optimizer set is preserved.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Keeping one basis optimal is different from keeping a fixed optimizer or the complete optimizer set, especially under degeneracy.

children.title: Individual Ranges versus Joint Changes
children.top_down_role: Distinction between one-at-a-time report intervals and simultaneous-change regions.

assumptions_latex: The LP is in equality form \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\), where \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full row rank.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\), fix an optimal basis matrix \(B\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}\) and let \(x_B=B^{-1}b\). A simultaneous right-hand-side perturbation \(\Delta b\in\mathbb R^m\) preserves primal feasibility of this basis exactly when \(x_B+B^{-1}\Delta b\ge0\); its dual feasibility is unchanged because only \(b\) varies. The individual range for coordinate \(i\) imposes this inequality with \(\Delta b=t e_i\) and all other perturbations zero. Even when every component of \(\Delta b\) lies in its individual interval, the combined vector \(B^{-1}\Delta b\) can make a basic component negative. Therefore the Cartesian product of the individual ranges is generally not a valid simultaneous-change region.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One-at-a-time right-hand-side ranges cannot generally be combined; simultaneous changes must satisfy the full basis-feasibility inequalities.

children.title: Continuous-LP Scope Boundary
children.top_down_role: Limits of classical LP ranging for discrete, conic, or materially nonlinear models.

knowledge_statements.title: Continuous-LP Scope Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary of basis-based ranging outside continuous polyhedral linear programs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the continuous LP \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\ge 0\}\), where \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\). Let \(\mathcal B\) be a basis index set, let \(B=A_{\mathcal B}\) be nonsingular, and let \(N\) be the complementary index set. Classical fixed-basis ranging uses \(B^{-1}b\ge0\) and \(c_N-A_N^{\mathsf T}B^{-\mathsf T}c_{\mathcal B}\ge0\), which certify primal and dual feasibility of this continuous-LP basis. They do not certify preservation of an optimizer after imposing integrality, replacing the polyhedral constraints by a nonpolyhedral cone, or introducing nonlinear objectives or constraints. For example, \(\min\{x:2x\ge1,\ 0\le x\le1\}\) has optimizer \(x=1/2\), whereas adding \(x\in\{0,1\}\) forces \(x=1\). Thus ranges computed from the relaxation need not describe the discrete solution or its value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fixed-basis ranges certify primal and dual feasibility for a continuous polyhedral LP basis; they do not extend unchanged to models with integrality, nonpolyhedral cones, or nonlinear structure.
assumptions_latex: The reported ranges are computed for a fixed basis \(B\) of a continuous standard-form LP.
Any additional discrete, conic, or nonlinear structure is absent from the basis-feasibility calculation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The classical fixed-basis range certificate does not extend unchanged to discrete, nonpolyhedral-conic, or materially nonlinear models.

children.title: Primal Degeneracy
children.top_down_role: Multiple basis descriptions and zero-length primal transitions.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal Degeneracy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Basis-relative degeneracy for an equality-form continuous LP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\ge 0\}\), where \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has row rank \(m\). A feasible basis \(B\) is primal degenerate when its basic solution \(x_B=B^{-1}b\) has at least one zero component. Thus fewer than \(m\) basic variables are strictly positive. The same feasible point may consequently admit several basis descriptions, and a simplex pivot can exchange basis indices while producing zero displacement in the primal point. Primal degeneracy concerns a basis representation and does not by itself imply that the primal optimal solution is nonunique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible basis is primal degenerate when some basic variable equals zero, permitting multiple basis descriptions or zero-displacement pivots without implying multiple primal optima.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) has full row rank.
\(B\) is a feasible basis.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The basis is primal degenerate exactly when \(\min_i (B^{-1}b)_i=0\).

notation.meaning: Nonsingular matrix formed by the basic columns of A.

children.title: Dual Degeneracy
children.top_down_role: Tied dual structures and nonunique dual transitions.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Degeneracy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Basis-relative dual degeneracy under the minimization reduced-cost convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\). Let \(\mathcal B\) be a basis index set, let \(B=A_{\mathcal B}\) be nonsingular, and let \(N\) be its complementary nonbasic index set. For a dual-feasible basis, define \(y=B^{-\mathsf T}c_{\mathcal B}\) and \(r_j=c_j-A_j^{\mathsf T}y\ge0\) for every \(j\in N\). The basis is dual degenerate when \(r_j=0\) for at least one \(j\in N\). Such a zero reduced cost creates a tied local optimality margin and may permit an alternative optimal basis transition, but it does not alone guarantee that the next basis is nonunique. Dual degeneracy is basis-relative and is distinct from nonuniqueness of the dual vector \(y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dual-feasible basis is dual degenerate when at least one nonbasic reduced cost is zero. This creates a tied optimality margin but does not by itself guarantee a nonunique transition or a nonunique dual vector.
assumptions_latex: \(B\) is nonsingular and dual feasible.
Reduced costs use the minimization convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Dual degeneracy holds exactly when there exists \(j\in N\) such that \(r_j=0\).

notation.meaning: Dual vector induced by the basis.
Reduced cost of nonbasic index j.

children.title: Multiple Primal Optima
children.top_down_role: Optimal faces and nonunique primal selections.

knowledge_statements.title: Multiple Primal Optima
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonuniqueness expressed as a positive-dimensional optimal face.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\) be nonempty and let \(v=\min_{x\in P}c^{\mathsf T}x\) be finite and attained. The primal optimal set is the exposed face \(F^*=\{x\in P:c^{\mathsf T}x=v\}\). The LP has multiple primal optima precisely when \(F^*\) contains two distinct points. In that case every convex combination \(\lambda x^1+(1-\lambda)x^2\), with \(x^1,x^2\in F^*\), \(x^1\ne x^2\), and \(0\le\lambda\le1\), is also optimal. A sensitivity calculation must therefore treat the primal optimizer as set-valued unless a selection rule is specified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multiple primal optima occur when the optimal face contains distinct feasible points; their entire connecting segment is optimal, so optimizer sensitivity is set-valued.
assumptions_latex: The feasible set is nonempty.
The optimal value is finite and attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Multiple primal optima exist if and only if \(|F^*|>1\).

children.title: Multiple Dual Optima
children.top_down_role: Alternative price systems and set-valued marginal information.

knowledge_statements.title: Multiple Dual Optima
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Alternative optimal prices and the resulting set-valued value derivative.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For fixed \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), define \(v(b)=\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\) and \(D=\{y\in\mathbb R^m:A^{\mathsf T}y\le c\}\). Suppose \(v\) is finite on a neighborhood of the reference \(b\) and the minimum at \(b\) is attained. Strong duality gives \(v(b)=\max_{y\in D}b^{\mathsf T}y\). The set \(Y^*(b)=\operatorname*{argmax}_{y\in D}b^{\mathsf T}y\) is the convex subdifferential \(\partial v(b)\). Thus distinct elements of \(Y^*(b)\) are alternative optimal price vectors, and if \(Y^*(b)\) contains at least two elements, the marginal-price information is set-valued and \(v\) is not differentiable at \(b\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the LP value is finite near the reference right-hand side, its optimal dual vectors form its subdifferential. Multiple optimal dual vectors therefore give set-valued marginal prices and imply nondifferentiability there.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) and \(c\) are fixed.
The value function \(v\) is finite on a neighborhood of \(b\).
The primal minimum at \(b\) is attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(|Y^*(b)|>1\), then the optimal dual price is nonunique and \(v\) is not differentiable at \(b\).

notation.meaning: Set of optimal dual vectors at right-hand side b.
Convex subdifferential of the primal value function.

children.title: Immediate Transition Event Family
children.top_down_role: Reference structures lying on immediate or multiple transition boundaries.

children.title: Zero-Width Sensitivity Ranges
children.top_down_role: Sensitivity ranges offering no nonzero perturbation interval around the reference structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Zero-Width Sensitivity Ranges
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Vanishing one-sided or two-sided basis-preserving parameter range.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a basis \(B\) in an affinely parameterized LP and a reference parameter \(\theta_0\). Its basis-preserving set is \(I_B=\{\theta:x_B(\theta)=B^{-1}b(\theta)\ge0,\ r_N(\theta)=c_N(\theta)-A_N^{\mathsf T}B^{-\mathsf T}c_B(\theta)\ge0\}\). A one-sided sensitivity width is zero when \(\theta_0\) is the corresponding endpoint of the maximal interval in \(I_B\) containing \(\theta_0\); it is zero in both directions when that interval is \(\{\theta_0\}\). Hence every perturbation in a zero-width direction violates at least one basis-feasibility inequality, although another optimal basis may still represent the same solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sensitivity width is zero when the current parameter is already an endpoint of its basis-valid interval; any movement in that direction invalidates the basis.
assumptions_latex: The right-hand side and objective coefficients depend affinely on one scalar parameter.
The matrix and candidate basis remain fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Zero width means no nonzero perturbation in the specified direction preserves both \(x_B(\theta)\ge0\) and \(r_N(\theta)\ge0\).

notation.meaning: Parameter set on which basis B is primal and dual feasible.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 7. Sensitivity and Parametric Analyses p. 109

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 7. Sensitivity and Parametric Analyses p. 109

children.title: Coincident Transition Events
children.top_down_role: Multiple structural transitions occurring at a common parameter value.

knowledge_statements.title: Coincident Transition Events
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Simultaneous activation of multiple basis-validity boundaries.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a fixed basis in a scalar affinely parameterized LP, let \(m_k(\theta)\) denote the basic-value and reduced-cost margins whose nonnegativity defines the basis-valid interval. Let \(\bar\theta\) be an endpoint approached from within that interval. Define \(K(\bar\theta)\) as the set of indices \(k\) for which \(m_k(\bar\theta)=0\) and \(m_k(\theta)>0\) at all sufficiently close interior points on the approach side. A coincident transition event occurs when \(|K(\bar\theta)|\ge2\). Several primal, dual, or mixed basis-validity boundaries then become active at the same parameter value, so a single strict ratio-test winner does not identify the transition. Additional pivot or tie-breaking analysis is required; coincidence alone does not guarantee that the next admissible basis is nonunique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Transition events coincide when at least two previously positive basis-validity margins become zero at the same endpoint. This creates a tie requiring further analysis but does not alone prove that the next basis is nonunique.
assumptions_latex: A fixed basis is valid on an interval approaching \(\bar\theta\).
The LP data depend affinely on the scalar parameter \(\theta\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A coincident transition event occurs exactly when \(|K(\bar\theta)|\ge2\).

notation.meaning: A basic-value or reduced-cost basis-feasibility margin.
Endpoint of the current basis-valid interval.
Margins that become active at the transition endpoint from the approach side.

source_refs.locator: 3. The Parametric Self-Dual Simplex Method p. 116

children.title: Immediate Boundary Exposure
children.top_down_role: Reference structures positioned directly on a sensitivity boundary.

knowledge_statements.title: Immediate Boundary Exposure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Directional test for leaving a basis-valid region immediately.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the fixed-basis validity conditions be differentiable margins \(m_k(\theta)\ge0\), and consider direction \(d\ne0\) from \(\theta_0\). The basis has immediate boundary exposure in direction \(d\) if some index \(k\) satisfies \(m_k(\theta_0)=0\) and \(\nabla m_k(\theta_0)^{\mathsf T}d<0\). Then \(m_k(\theta_0+t d)<0\) for all sufficiently small \(t>0\), so the current basis ceases immediately to be primal or dual feasible in that direction. The condition concerns basis preservation; the LP solution or optimal value may remain unchanged through a degenerate basis exchange.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A basis is immediately exposed when an already active validity margin has a negative directional derivative, making every sufficiently small step violate that margin.
assumptions_latex: The basis-validity margins are differentiable at \(\theta_0\).
The perturbation follows direction \(d\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(m_k(\theta_0)=0\) and \(\nabla m_k(\theta_0)^{\mathsf T}d<0\), the basis is invalid for every sufficiently small positive step along \(d\).

notation.meaning: A primal or dual basis-feasibility margin.

children.title: Finite-Optimum Transition Boundary
children.top_down_role: Boundary behavior where perturbations leave the finite-optimum regime.

children.title: Loss of Primal Feasibility
children.top_down_role: Perturbations crossing from feasible to infeasible parameter regimes.

knowledge_statements.title: Loss of Primal Feasibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Crossing a parameter boundary where the primal feasible set becomes empty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(P(\theta)=\{x\ge0:Ax=b(\theta)\}\), a parameter path loses primal feasibility at \(\bar\theta\) in direction \(d\) when \(P(\bar\theta)\ne\varnothing\) but \(P(\bar\theta+t d)=\varnothing\) for all sufficiently small \(t>0\). By Farkas' alternative, each infeasible parameter admits a vector \(y_t\) satisfying \(A^{\mathsf T}y_t\ge0\) and \(b(\bar\theta+t d)^{\mathsf T}y_t<0\). This certificate separates the perturbed right-hand side from the cone generated by the columns of \(A\), establishing that no nonnegative primal solution exists beyond the boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Primal feasibility is lost when an infinitesimal parameter crossing empties the feasible set; a Farkas vector certifies each infeasible perturbed instance.
assumptions_latex: The constraint matrix is fixed.
The right-hand side varies continuously along the parameter path.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Beyond the boundary, primal infeasibility is certified by \(A^{\mathsf T}y_t\ge0\) and \(b(\bar\theta+t d)^{\mathsf T}y_t<0\).

notation.meaning: Primal feasible set at parameter theta.

source_refs.locator: 6.2 Primal-Dual Relationships p. 264

source_witnesses.locator: 6.2 Primal-Dual Relationships p. 264

children.title: Loss of Dual Feasibility
children.top_down_role: Perturbations crossing toward primal-unbounded regimes.

knowledge_statements.title: Loss of Dual Feasibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Crossing toward primal unboundedness when the dual feasible set disappears.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the primal-dual pair \(\min\{c(\theta)^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\) and \(D(\theta)=\{y:A^{\mathsf T}y\le c(\theta)\}\), dual feasibility is lost at \(\bar\theta\) in direction \(d\) when \(D(\bar\theta)\ne\varnothing\) but \(D(\bar\theta+t d)=\varnothing\) for all sufficiently small \(t>0\). If the corresponding primal feasible set remains nonempty, every such perturbed problem is primal unbounded below. Equivalently, it admits a recession direction \(q_t\ge0\) with \(Aq_t=0\) and \(c(\bar\theta+t d)^{\mathsf T}q_t<0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dual feasibility is lost when the dual set becomes empty after crossing; if primal feasibility persists, a negative-cost recession direction proves primal unboundedness.
assumptions_latex: The constraint matrix and right-hand side are fixed.
The objective varies continuously along the parameter path.
Primal feasibility persists after the crossing.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Dual infeasibility together with primal feasibility implies primal unboundedness, certified by \(q_t\ge0\), \(Aq_t=0\), and \(c(\bar\theta+t d)^{\mathsf T}q_t<0\).

notation.meaning: Dual feasible set at parameter theta.
Negative-cost primal recession direction after crossing.

children.title: Indeterminate Status Boundary Family
children.top_down_role: Boundary regimes with numerically delicate status classification.

children.title: Weak Status Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Transition boundaries supported by numerically delicate status evidence.

knowledge_statements.title: Weak Status Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Status changes controlled by a certificate having zero boundary margin.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A parametric LP has a weak status boundary at \(\bar\theta\) when a separating or recession certificate is valid only with zero decisive margin there but acquires a strict margin on one side. For right-hand-side feasibility, this occurs when some \(y\) satisfies \(A^{\mathsf T}y\ge0\), \(b(\bar\theta)^{\mathsf T}y=0\), and \(b(\bar\theta+t d)^{\mathsf T}y<0\) for all sufficiently small \(t>0\). The analogous unboundedness boundary has \(q\ge0\), \(Aq=0\), \(c(\bar\theta)^{\mathsf T}q=0\), and \(c(\bar\theta+t d)^{\mathsf T}q<0\). Exact zero margin makes status classification sensitive at the boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A weak status boundary occurs when an infeasibility or unboundedness certificate has zero decisive margin at the boundary and becomes strict immediately beyond it.
assumptions_latex: LP data vary continuously along direction \(d\).
The displayed certificate is nonzero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A zero certificate margin at \(\bar\theta\) can become a strict infeasibility or unboundedness certificate under arbitrarily small directed perturbations.

source_refs.locator: 6.2 Primal-Dual Relationships p. 264
