children.title: Ambiguous Status Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Transition boundaries admitting uncertain finite, infeasible, or unbounded classification.

knowledge_statements.title: Ambiguous Status Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Neighborhood-level ambiguity between distinct exact LP status regions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Theta_F\), \(\Theta_I\), and \(\Theta_U\) denote parameter regions where an LP respectively has a finite optimum, is primal infeasible, or is primal unbounded. A parameter \(\bar\theta\) is an ambiguous status boundary when it lies in \(\overline{\Theta_S}\cap\overline{\Theta_T}\) for two distinct statuses \(S\ne T\). Equivalently, there exist sequences \(\theta_k\to\bar\theta\) and \(\eta_k\to\bar\theta\) whose exact statuses are \(S\) and \(T\), respectively. The LP at \(\bar\theta\) still has an exact status, but no neighborhood of it has a unique status; finite-precision perturbations can therefore produce different classifications.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A status boundary is ambiguous when arbitrarily close exact instances have different statuses, although the boundary instance itself still has one exact mathematical status.
assumptions_latex: Each parameter specifies a finite-dimensional continuous LP.
Status regions are classified in exact arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\bar\theta\in\overline{\Theta_S}\cap\overline{\Theta_T}\) with \(S\ne T\), every neighborhood of \(\bar\theta\) contains instances with different exact statuses.

source_refs.locator: 3. The Parametric Self-Dual Simplex Method p. 116

source_witnesses.locator: 3. The Parametric Self-Dual Simplex Method p. 116

children.title: Tolerance-Sensitive Classification
children.top_down_role: Boundary classifications that vary with numerical tolerances.

assumptions_latex: The solver applies fixed absolute or relative feasibility and optimality tolerances collected in \(\tau\).
The reported status is computed from finite-precision residuals and certificates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal S_\tau(d)\) is tolerance-sensitive at \(d\) if there exist admissible \(\tau_1,\tau_2\) with \(\mathcal S_{\tau_1}(d)\ne\mathcal S_{\tau_2}(d)\).

notation.meaning: status returned under tolerance vector tau

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: operational definition of tolerance-sensitive solver classification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational boundary for finite-precision LP status reports; it does not redefine exact feasibility or boundedness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For LP data \(d=(A,b,c)\), let \(\mathcal S_\tau(d)\) denote the status returned when feasibility, optimality, and certificate tests use tolerance vector \(\tau\). The classification is tolerance-sensitive at \(d\) when
\[\exists\,\tau_1,\tau_2\in\mathcal T:\quad \mathcal S_{\tau_1}(d)\ne\mathcal S_{\tau_2}(d).\]
Thus the tolerance-sensitive boundary is the set of data for which changing admissible numerical thresholds changes the reported status, although the exact mathematical LP is unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A classification is tolerance-sensitive when two admissible tolerance settings assign different solver statuses to the same exact LP data.
knowledge_statements.title: Tolerance-Sensitive Classification

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits, but the admissible set \(\mathcal T\) is undefined and no source supports a solver-independent status-boundary formulation.

children.title: Finite-Precision Sensitivity
children.top_down_role: Numerical effects on computed ranges, prices, breakpoints, and region classifications.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Solver Parameters to Manage Numerical Issues

children.title: Ill-Conditioned Bases
children.top_down_role: Unstable basis solves affecting range and price information.

assumptions_latex: \(B\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}\) is a nonsingular basis matrix.
Perturbations are measured in a subordinate matrix norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\kappa(B)\varepsilon\) is not small, computed basic values and simplex prices may be unreliable even when residuals are small.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order conditioning of simplex basis solves used in ranging and shadow-price calculations.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 7. Sensitivity and Parametric Analyses p. 109

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A basis \(B\) is ill-conditioned when \(\kappa(B)=\lVert B\rVert\lVert B^{-1}\rVert\) is large. For sufficiently small perturbations \(\Delta B\) and \(\Delta b\), the basic solution \(x_B=B^{-1}b\) has first-order relative sensitivity proportional to \(\kappa(B)\). The same amplification affects the price solve \(B^{\mathsf T}y=c_B\). Consequently, when \(\kappa(B)\varepsilon\) is not small, finite-precision basic values, reduced costs, allowable ranges, and shadow prices can change substantially under perturbations of relative size \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A poorly conditioned basis amplifies small data and rounding errors in basic-value and price solves, making ranges and shadow prices numerically unstable.
knowledge_statements.title: Ill-Conditioned Bases

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 7. Sensitivity and Parametric Analyses p. 109

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property fits the leaf, but the cited general sensitivity section does not clearly support the numerical-conditioning claims. Relative sensitivity is bounded in terms of condition numbers under explicit perturbation hypotheses, not simply proportional to \(\kappa(B)\); the price solve may involve \(\kappa(B^{\mathsf T})\) for the chosen norm.

children.title: Near-Degeneracy
children.top_down_role: Small structural margins causing unstable basis and breakpoint identification.

assumptions_latex: A primal-dual basic solution is available for an LP in standard form.
Residual and margin comparisons use a fixed norm and consistent scaling.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Near-degeneracy occurs when \(\delta=\min\{\min_{i\in B}x_i,\min_{j\notin B}|\bar c_j|\}\) is small relative to the data scale.

notation.meaning: reduced cost of nonbasic variable j
smallest primal or dual basis margin

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Numerical near-degeneracy measured by small primal or dual margins at a basic optimum.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 7. Sensitivity and Parametric Analyses p. 109

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a primal-dual basic optimum with basic set \(B\), define
\[\delta=\min\!\left\{\min_{i\in B}x_i,\;\min_{j\notin B}|\bar c_j|\right\}.\]
After consistent normalization, the solution is near-degenerate at scale \(\eta>0\) when \(\delta\le\eta\). A small basic variable permits an imminent primal basis change, while a small nonbasic reduced cost permits an imminent dual basis change. Hence perturbations comparable to \(\delta\) can alter the selected basis or the first identified parametric breakpoint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An optimum is near-degenerate when some basic variable or nonbasic reduced cost has a very small margin, so tiny perturbations can change the basis.
knowledge_statements.title: Near-Degeneracy

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 7. Sensitivity and Parametric Analyses p. 109

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role fits, but the proposed \(\delta\) directly combines primal-variable and reduced-cost quantities with different units. A source-backed normalization and objective-sign convention are needed before the formula is reliable.

children.title: Solver Status Tolerance System
children.top_down_role: Tolerance-dependent classification of feasibility, activity, and optimality.

children.title: Feasibility Tolerances
children.top_down_role: Numerical thresholds affecting feasibility or activity classification.

assumptions_latex: The primal LP is \(Ax=b\) with \(x\ge0\).
Residuals are evaluated after choosing explicit row and variable scaling.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The point is tolerance-feasible exactly when \(\rho_p(x)\le\tau_p\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: normalized residual predicate for numerical primal feasibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic normalized feasibility test; individual solvers may use different rowwise denominators and norms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(Ax=b\), \(x\ge0\), define the normalized primal infeasibility
\[\rho_p(x)=\max\!\left\{\frac{\lVert Ax-b\rVert_\infty}{1+\lVert A\rVert_\infty\lVert x\rVert_\infty+\lVert b\rVert_\infty},\;\frac{\lVert(-x)_+\rVert_\infty}{1+\lVert x\rVert_\infty}\right\}.\]
Given \(\tau_p\ge0\), the point \(x\) is tolerance-feasible precisely when \(\rho_p(x)\le\tau_p\). This predicate concerns numerical acceptance and need not imply exact feasibility when \(\tau_p>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A point is numerically feasible when its normalized equality and nonnegativity violations do not exceed the chosen feasibility tolerance.
knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility Tolerances

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: This is a plausible condition, but the particular normalization is an invented convention rather than a universal feasibility tolerance. Dimensions for \(A,b,x\) and a source for the selected residual convention are required.

children.title: Optimality Tolerances
children.top_down_role: Numerical thresholds affecting reduced-cost or optimality classification.

assumptions_latex: The primal-dual pair is in standard form with dual slack \(s=c-A^{\mathsf T}y\).
The candidate satisfies the selected numerical primal-feasibility test.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The candidate is tolerance-optimal when \(\rho_d(y,s)\le\tau_d\) and \(\rho_\mu(x,s)\le\tau_\mu\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic primal-dual optimality acceptance test rather than a solver-specific stopping rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(s=c-A^{\mathsf T}y\). Define
\[\rho_d(y,s)=\frac{\lVert A^{\mathsf T}y+s-c\rVert_\infty+\lVert(-s)_+\rVert_\infty}{1+\lVert A\rVert_\infty\lVert y\rVert_\infty+\lVert s\rVert_\infty+\lVert c\rVert_\infty},\qquad \rho_\mu(x,s)=\frac{|x^{\mathsf T}s|}{1+|c^{\mathsf T}x|+|b^{\mathsf T}y|}.\]
For tolerances \(\tau_d,\tau_\mu\ge0\), a primal-feasible candidate is tolerance-optimal when \(\rho_d(y,s)\le\tau_d\) and \(\rho_\mu(x,s)\le\tau_\mu\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible candidate is numerically optimal when normalized dual infeasibility and complementarity are both within their prescribed tolerances.
knowledge_statements.title: Optimality Tolerances

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role fits, but the primal objective sense and dimensions are absent. Because \(s=c-A^{\mathsf T}y\) is imposed, the equality-residual term in \(\rho_d\) vanishes identically; a source-backed computed-slack convention is needed.

children.title: Tolerance-Induced Status Changes
children.top_down_role: Changes in reported sensitivity status caused by tolerance choices.

assumptions_latex: A status rule compares continuous residual measures with tolerance thresholds.
The exact LP data remain fixed while at least one tolerance varies.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A reported status can change only when a threshold crosses an attained residual or certificate margin, or when finite-precision iteration changes the candidate tested.

notation.meaning: vector of computed residual and certificate measures

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: threshold-crossing characterization of tolerance-induced classification changes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Status transitions caused by numerical decision thresholds, distinct from transitions in the exact LP solution set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose a deterministic status test assigns \(\mathcal S_\tau(d)=\Phi(r(d),\tau)\) by finitely many comparisons of the form \(r_k(d)\le\tau_k\). With the computed candidate fixed, \(\mathcal S_\tau(d)\) is locally constant in \(\tau\) away from
\[\bigcup_k\{\tau:r_k(d)=\tau_k\}.\]
Therefore a tolerance-induced status change requires crossing one of these comparison boundaries. In an iterative solver, changing \(\tau\) may additionally change termination and hence the candidate whose residuals or certificates are classified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solver status is locally stable between tolerance thresholds but may change when a residual crosses a threshold or termination selects a different candidate.
knowledge_statements.title: Tolerance-Induced Status Changes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits. The threshold-crossing result is valid only for the stipulated fixed-candidate finite-comparison model, but no source establishes that model or its relationship to actual solver status systems.

children.title: Model-Transformation Sensitivity Interface
children.top_down_role: Dependence of reported structures on scaling and transformed model representations.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Presolve and numerical issue guidance

children.title: Scaling Effects
children.top_down_role: Changes in reported sensitivity structures attributable to numerical rescaling.

assumptions_latex: Positive diagonal matrices \(D_r\) and \(D_c\) scale rows and variables.
Reported residuals are tested in the scaled formulation with fixed absolute tolerances.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact feasibility and optimal value are preserved by the variable correspondence, but absolute residual tests and numerical sensitivity measures are generally not invariant.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: exact diagonal scaling equivalence and noninvariance of absolute numerical tests
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact diagonal equivalence versus finite-precision and fixed-tolerance noninvariance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For positive diagonal \(D_r,D_c\), the system \(Ax=b\), \(x\ge0\), with objective \(c^{\mathsf T}x\), is represented after \(x=D_cz\) by
\[(D_rAD_c)z=D_rb,\qquad z\ge0,\qquad (D_c^{\mathsf T}c)^{\mathsf T}z.\]
This bijection preserves exact feasibility and objective values. However, the scaled residual is \(D_r(Ax-b)\), so a fixed absolute residual tolerance is not invariant under \(D_r\). Conditioning, recovered reduced costs, and reported allowable ranges can likewise depend on scaling and finite-precision unscaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Diagonal scaling preserves the exact LP, but fixed numerical tolerances, conditioning, reduced costs, and reported ranges can change with the chosen scaling.
knowledge_statements.title: Scaling Effects

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits and the exact diagonal transformation is plausible, but dimensions and a source supporting the claims about recovered reduced costs, allowable ranges, and finite-precision unscaling are missing.

children.title: Presolve Effects
children.top_down_role: Changes arising from elimination, substitution, aggregation, or bound tightening during presolve.

assumptions_latex: Presolve applies transformations that are exact and reversible on the retained feasible set.
Sensitivity information is initially computed for the reduced LP.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Reduced-model ranges and multipliers are valid for original rows or columns only after applying the transformation-specific postsolve map.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: presolve changes the coordinate system of sensitivity information
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Effect of exact presolve transformations on the interpretation of basis-oriented postoptimal reports.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let presolve map original data \(d\) to reduced data \(\widehat d\) and retain reconstruction information \(P\). Even when \(P\) gives an exact correspondence between feasible solutions and preserves the optimum, a reduced row, column, or basis need not correspond one-to-one to an original model object. Therefore multipliers, reduced costs, and one-at-a-time parameter ranges computed for \(\widehat d\) cannot generally be attached directly to \(d\); they require the transformation-specific inverse or adjoint postsolve mapping encoded by \(P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Presolve can merge, remove, or substitute model objects, so reduced-model prices and ranges require transformation-specific reconstruction before original-model interpretation.
knowledge_statements.title: Presolve Effects

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property kind fits, but presolve transformations need not furnish a one-to-one correspondence of original and reduced model objects. A transformation-specific source is needed to substantiate the asserted inverse or adjoint mapping of multipliers, reduced costs, and ranges.

children.title: Postsolve Structure Recovery
children.top_down_role: Interpretive limits when sensitivity information is mapped back to the original model representation.

assumptions_latex: Each presolve transformation records an exact reconstruction rule.
A primal-dual solution and any available basis information are given for the reduced LP.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is an original-space primal-dual solution with mapped statuses; a basis report is emitted only if the reconstructed statuses form a valid nonsingular basis.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: reverse application of recorded presolve transformations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract postsolve algorithm for primal-dual and basis-oriented sensitivity structures.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input recorded transformations \(P_1,\ldots,P_k\) and a reduced solution \((\widehat x,\widehat y,\widehat s)\). Initialize \((x^{(k)},y^{(k)},s^{(k)})=(\widehat x,\widehat y,\widehat s)\). For \(i=k,k-1,\ldots,1\), apply the reconstruction rule of \(P_i\) to obtain \((x^{(i-1)},y^{(i-1)},s^{(i-1)})\) and map row, column, and basis statuses. Output \((x^{(0)},y^{(0)},s^{(0)})\). Output basis-dependent ranges only if the recovered basic columns are nonsingular and the reconstructed primal-dual signs satisfy the selected tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Postsolve reverses recorded presolve transformations, reconstructs primal-dual values and statuses, and reports basis ranges only when the recovered basis is valid.
knowledge_statements.title: Postsolve Structure Recovery

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind is appropriate, but the abstract reverse-reconstruction procedure and the conditions for recovering a valid basis and basis-dependent ranges require a specific postsolve reference.

children.title: Scaling–Presolve Interaction
children.top_down_role: Combined influence of rescaling plus model transformation on reported bases, dual values, or allowable ranges.

assumptions_latex: Scaling and presolve are exact transformations in exact arithmetic.
Finite-precision presolve decisions use scaled residuals or coefficient thresholds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Scaling and presolve need not commute numerically, so their composition can produce different reduced structures and sensitivity reports.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: thresholded presolve decisions are scale-dependent
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Noncommutation caused by finite-precision, threshold-based presolve decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(S\) be diagonal scaling and \(P_\tau\) a presolve operator whose eliminations depend on coefficient or residual comparisons with \(\tau\). In exact symbolic arithmetic the resulting LPs may be equivalent, but generally
\[P_\tau(S(d))\ne S(P_\tau(d))\]
as computational representations, because scaling changes the quantities compared with \(\tau\). Consequently the two orders can retain different rows or columns, recover different bases, and yield different finite-precision ranges or prices, even when both postsolved solutions satisfy the original model tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Threshold-based presolve is scale-dependent, so changing transformation order can alter the reduced structure, recovered basis, and numerical sensitivity report.
knowledge_statements.title: Scaling–Presolve Interaction

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role is suitable, but \(P_\tau\) and the comparison conventions are underspecified, and no source supports the claimed scale-dependent noncommutation and downstream sensitivity effects.

children.title: Basis Recovery after Interior-Point Solution
children.top_down_role: Relationship between basis-free optimal information and basis-oriented ranging reports.

assumptions_latex: A primal-dual interior-point iterate is sufficiently close to an LP optimum.
A crossover procedure can perform stable linear solves and simplex pivots.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Crossover returns a primal-dual feasible basic optimum when recovery succeeds; basis-dependent ranges are undefined until such a basis is selected.

notation.meaning: interior-point primal, dual, and slack estimates

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Crossover from a basis-free interior-point solution to a basis supporting classical ranging reports.

source_refs.locator: Moving to a Solution from an Interior Point p. 55
3.3.5 A rounding procedure for interior-point solutions p. 62
source_refs.source_title: Interior Point Methods for Linear Optimization

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a near-optimal interior-point triple \((x,y,s)\). Select candidate basic indices using large primal components, small dual slacks, and rank tests; complete them to a nonsingular set \(B\). Solve \(A_Bx_B=b\) and \(A_B^{\mathsf T}y=c_B\), compute nonbasic reduced costs, and pivot until primal and dual feasibility hold within prescribed tolerances. Output the basic optimum and \(B\). Classical one-at-a-time ranges are attached to this recovered basis; before crossover, the interior-point solution alone does not select a unique basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Crossover selects and repairs a nonsingular basis from a near-optimal interior-point solution; classical basis ranges become available only after successful recovery.
knowledge_statements.title: Basis Recovery after Interior-Point Solution

children.title: Interpretive Failure Modes
children.top_down_role: Misuses that extend valid local information beyond its structural domain.

children.title: Independent-Range Aggregation Failure
children.top_down_role: Invalid combination of separately computed one-at-a-time ranges.

assumptions_latex: One-at-a-time objective-coefficient ranges are computed while all other coefficients remain at baseline values.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Combining separately admissible values \(c_1=1.1\) and \(c_2=1.9\) changes the optimal basis, despite each value lying in its individual baseline range.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete failure of treating one-at-a-time objective ranges as a jointly admissible box.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 7. Sensitivity and Parametric Analyses p. 109

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider
\[\max\{c_1x_1+c_2x_2:x_1+x_2\le1,\ x_1,x_2\ge0\}\]
at \(c^0=(2,1)\), whose unique optimum is \((1,0)\). Holding \(c_2=1\), this basis remains optimal for \(c_1\ge1\). Holding \(c_1=2\), it remains optimal for \(c_2\le2\). Thus \(c_1=1.1\) and \(c_2=1.9\) are separately admissible. Applied together, however, \(c_2>c_1\), so the unique optimum becomes \((0,1)\). The Cartesian product of independent ranges is therefore not a joint stability region.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two coefficient changes can each lie within its one-at-a-time range yet jointly switch the optimal basis, so independent ranges cannot be aggregated.
knowledge_statements.title: Independent-Range Aggregation Failure

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 7. Sensitivity and Parametric Analyses p. 109

children.title: Shadow-Price Extrapolation Failure
children.top_down_role: Use of local marginal values beyond their applicable structural regime.

knowledge_statements.title: Shadow-Price Extrapolation Failure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete right-hand-side example showing failure beyond the current basis-validity interval.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(v(b)=\max\{x:0\le x\le b,\ x\le1\}\) at \(b_0=1/2\). The unique optimum is \(x^*=1/2\), and the shadow price of the constraint \(x\le b\) is \(y^*=1\). For every sufficiently small perturbation \(\Delta b\) with \(b_0+\Delta b<1\), the local formula \(v(b_0+\Delta b)=v(b_0)+y^*\Delta b\) is exact. Extrapolating it to \(b=2\) predicts \(v(2)=2\), whereas the unchanged constraint \(x\le1\) gives \(v(2)=1\). Thus a shadow price need not remain valid after the active set or optimal basis changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A shadow price is locally exact only while the supporting basis remains valid; extrapolation across an active-set change can give the wrong optimal value.
assumptions_latex: The shadow price is computed at \(b_0=1/2\).

notation.meaning: Optimal value at right-hand side b.
Local shadow price of the parameterized constraint.

children.title: Basis-to-Face Inference Failure
children.top_down_role: Conflation of a selected basis with the complete set of optimal solutions.

children.title: Selected Basis Representation
children.top_down_role: Solver-reported information tied to one basic representation of an optimal solution.

knowledge_statements.title: Selected Basis Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representation of one optimal basic feasible solution in standard-form maximization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\max\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\), choose an index set \(B\) of \(m\) linearly independent columns and let \(N\) be its complement. The basis represents the basic solution \(x_B=A_B^{-1}b\), \(x_N=0\), together with the multiplier \(y=A_B^{-\mathsf T}c_B\). It is primal feasible when \(x_B\ge0\) and optimal when the nonbasic reduced costs satisfy \(c_N-A_N^{\mathsf T}y\le0\). This representation selects one basic optimal point and associated tableau data; it does not itself describe every point of a positive-dimensional optimal face.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An optimal basis encodes one basic optimal solution, its multiplier, and reduced costs, but generally not the entire optimal face.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has row rank \(m\).
\(A_B\) is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_B=A_B^{-1}b\ge0\) and \(c_N-A_N^{\mathsf T}A_B^{-\mathsf T}c_B\le0\) imply that the represented basic solution is optimal.

notation.meaning: Basic and nonbasic column index sets.
Dual multiplier represented by the selected basis.

children.title: Complete Optimal Face
children.top_down_role: Structural information belonging to the full collection of alternative optimal solutions.

knowledge_statements.title: Complete Optimal Face
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimal face of a feasible polyhedron for a finite-valued linear program.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax\le b\}\) be nonempty and let \(v=\max_{x\in P}c^{\mathsf T}x\) be finite and attained. The complete optimal face is \[F^*=\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in P}c^{\mathsf T}x=\{x\in P:c^{\mathsf T}x=v\}.\] It is an exposed face of \(P\): if \(z=\lambda x+(1-\lambda)y\in F^*\), where \(x,y\in P\) and \(0<\lambda<1\), then \(x,y\in F^*\). The set includes all optimal vertices, their feasible convex combinations, and any nonvertex optimal points; a selected optimal basis generally represents only one member.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The complete optimal face is the set of all feasible points attaining the optimal value, including optimal vertices and their feasible convex combinations.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is a nonempty polyhedron.
The maximum of \(c^{\mathsf T}x\) over \(P\) is finite and attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F^*=P\cap\{x:c^{\mathsf T}x=v\}\) is an exposed face of \(P\).

children.title: Basis-to-Face Inference Failure
children.top_down_role: Invalid conclusions about the full optimal set drawn from properties of one selected basis.

knowledge_statements.title: Basis-to-Face Inference Failure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A selected optimal basis fails to determine a positive-dimensional optimal face.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\max\{x_1+x_2:x_1+x_2+s=1,\ x_1,x_2,s\ge0\}\). Selecting \(x_1\) as the basic variable yields the optimal basic feasible solution \((x_1,x_2,s)=(1,0,0)\). Nevertheless, the complete optimal face is \[F^*=\{(x_1,x_2,0):x_1,x_2\ge0,\ x_1+x_2=1\},\] which contains infinitely many points and also the distinct optimal basic feasible solution \((0,1,0)\). Hence tableau information from the selected basis cannot justify the inference that its represented point is the unique optimum or that it describes the complete optimal face.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One optimal basis may identify only an endpoint of an optimal edge, so basis data cannot establish uniqueness or recover the whole face.
assumptions_latex: The linear program is written with slack variable \(s\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{(1,0,0)\}\subsetneq F^*\), so the selected basis representation is not the complete optimal set.

notation.meaning: Set of all optimal feasible solutions.

children.title: Alternative Optimal Bases
children.top_down_role: Distinct basis representations associated with the same objective value or optimal face.

knowledge_statements.title: Alternative Optimal Bases
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relation between zero reduced costs, adjacent optimal pivots, and optimal-face representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a feasible optimal basis of \(\max\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\), suppose a nonbasic variable \(x_j\) has reduced cost \(\bar c_j=0\). If its tableau direction admits a positive ratio-test step, pivoting \(x_j\) into the basis produces a distinct adjacent optimal basic feasible solution; the objective is unchanged along the intervening feasible edge. If the allowable step is zero, the pivot may instead produce an alternative optimal basis representing the same degenerate vertex. Thus alternative optimal bases may reveal optimal-face structure, but neither their existence nor a list obtained from one tableau automatically enumerates every point of the complete optimal face.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A zero-reduced-cost pivot can produce another optimal vertex or merely another basis for the same degenerate vertex; it does not enumerate the full face.
assumptions_latex: The current basis is primal feasible and optimal.
A nonbasic variable has zero reduced cost.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A feasible pivot on the zero-reduced-cost variable preserves the objective value, but its new basis need not represent a distinct point.

notation.meaning: Reduced cost of nonbasic variable j.

children.title: Postoptimal-Decision Design Boundary
children.top_down_role: Conflation of postoptimal dependence with robust or stochastic decision design.

children.title: Postoptimal Sensitivity
children.top_down_role: Dependence of an existing LP solution structure on parameter perturbations.

knowledge_statements.title: Postoptimal Sensitivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local right-hand-side sensitivity while one optimal basis remains primal feasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(v(t)=\max\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b+t d,\ x\ge0\}\), and suppose basis \(B\) is optimal at \(t=0\). Because reduced costs are unchanged by this right-hand-side perturbation, the same basis remains optimal for every \(t\) in the interval \(I=\{t:A_B^{-1}(b+t d)\ge0\}\). On \(I\), \[x_B(t)=A_B^{-1}(b+t d),\qquad v(t)=v(0)+t\,y^{\mathsf T}d,\qquad y=A_B^{-\mathsf T}c_B.\] The multiplier therefore gives an exact local marginal value only on this basis-validity interval; outside it, reoptimization or a new parametric segment is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Postoptimal sensitivity gives exact affine changes while the current basis stays feasible and optimal; crossing its validity interval requires a new basis.
assumptions_latex: \(A_B\) is nonsingular.
Basis \(B\) is optimal at \(t=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(t\in I\), \(v(t)=v(0)+t y^{\mathsf T}d\).

notation.meaning: Parameter interval on which the basis remains primal feasible.
Dual multiplier associated with the basis.

children.title: Robust Optimization
children.top_down_role: Decision design against explicitly represented uncertainty sets.

knowledge_statements.title: Robust Optimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Static robust counterpart for a family of uncertain linear constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U\) be a prescribed uncertainty set and let the linear data be \((c(u),A(u),b(u))\) for \(u\in U\). A static robust solution is chosen before \(u\) is observed and solves \[\min_{x\in X}\ \sup_{u\in U}c(u)^{\mathsf T}x\quad\text{subject to}\quad A(u)x\ge b(u)\ \text{for every }u\in U.\] Unlike nominal postoptimal sensitivity, this formulation requires simultaneous feasibility over the full uncertainty set and optimizes worst-case performance. Its solution need not coincide with a nominal optimizer adjusted using local shadow prices, even when every individual realization defines a linear program.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Static robust optimization chooses one decision that is feasible for every modeled realization and minimizes worst-case cost, rather than extrapolating nominal sensitivities.
assumptions_latex: \(U\ne\varnothing\).
The decision set \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is fixed before uncertainty is observed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Any robust-feasible \(x\) satisfies \(A(u)x\ge b(u)\) simultaneously for all \(u\in U\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The selected static robust formulation is mathematically coherent and appropriately distinguished from nominal sensitivity, but the record supplies no citation. An authoritative robust-optimization source with a specific section, theorem, definition, or page locator is required to support this exact uncertainty-set, here-and-now, worst-case formulation.

children.title: Stochastic Optimization
children.top_down_role: Decision design using probability-based representations of uncertain quantities.

knowledge_statements.title: Stochastic Optimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Risk-neutral one-stage stochastic linear optimization with almost-sure feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On a probability space carrying random data \(\xi\), a risk-neutral one-stage stochastic linear program chooses a deterministic decision before observing \(\xi\) and solves \[\min_{x\in X}\ \mathbb E[c(\xi)^{\mathsf T}x]\quad\text{subject to}\quad A(\xi)x\ge b(\xi)\ \text{almost surely}.\] The expectation must be well defined for admissible decisions. This model aggregates outcomes by their probability law rather than using only nominal derivatives or requiring feasibility for every element of a deterministic uncertainty set. Other information structures, recourse decisions, or risk measures define different stochastic models and cannot be inferred from local LP sensitivity alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One-stage stochastic optimization selects a pre-observation decision using a probability distribution, expected cost, and almost-sure constraints; local nominal sensitivity does not define that policy.
assumptions_latex: \(\xi\) is a random element with a specified probability law.
\(\mathbb E[|c(\xi)^{\mathsf T}x|]<\infty\) for every admissible \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A feasible decision satisfies \(\mathbb P(A(\xi)x\ge b(\xi))=1\) and is evaluated by \(\mathbb E[c(\xi)^{\mathsf T}x]\).

notation.meaning: Expectation under the specified probability law.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The one-stage risk-neutral model is internally coherent and explicitly separated from recourse and alternative risk measures, but no source is cited. An authoritative stochastic-programming source with a specific locator is required for this exact pre-observation, expected-cost, almost-sure-feasibility variant.

children.title: Local-to-Uncertain-Regime Extrapolation
children.top_down_role: Misuse of local sensitivity information as a substitute for uncertainty-aware decision design.

knowledge_statements.title: Local-to-Uncertain-Regime Extrapolation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between nominal differential information and optimization over an uncertainty regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(v(t)\) be the optimal value of a parametric linear program and suppose a nominal basis yields \(v(t)=v(0)+t g\) only for \(t\in I\), where \(I\) is its basis-validity interval. For an uncertainty set \(U\not\subseteq I\), the scalar \(g\) does not determine \(\sup_{t\in U}v(t)\), \(\mathbb E[v(T)]\), or a decision feasible for every \(t\in U\). Breakpoints outside \(I\), probability weights, and the timing of decisions can change each quantity. Consequently, replacing the uncertain regime by the extrapolation \(v(0)+t g\) is justified only after establishing validity throughout the relevant support and matching the intended robust or stochastic criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nominal derivative cannot determine worst-case or expected performance when uncertainty crosses basis breakpoints or changes the decision’s information structure.
assumptions_latex: \(v(t)=v(0)+tg\) has been established only for \(t\in I\).
The uncertainty regime contains parameter values outside \(I\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Local sensitivity \(g\) alone is insufficient to determine uncertain-regime feasibility or objective values.

children.title: Policy Redesign Boundary
children.top_down_role: Boundary between interpreting parameter dependence for a fixed model structure versus redesigning decisions for uncertain conditions.

knowledge_statements.title: Policy Redesign Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Criterion separating valid postoptimal updates from decisions requiring a redesigned optimization model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A postoptimal update is valid when the contemplated parameter values remain within a certified critical region, the feasible set and objective retain the modeled form, and the decision is made under the same information structure as in the nominal linear program. If any of these conditions fails—particularly when uncertainty spans several basis regions, feasibility must hold simultaneously across scenarios, or recourse becomes available after observation—the nominal basis and its shadow prices do not specify an admissible policy. The optimization problem must then be reformulated and solved with the appropriate robust, stochastic, multistage, or other decision structure rather than treated as a sensitivity calculation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sensitivity updates suffice only within the certified nominal structure; broader uncertainty, changed feasibility requirements, or new decision timing requires model and policy redesign.
assumptions_latex: A nominal linear program and its local sensitivity region are available.
A proposed operating regime or information structure is specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Leaving the certified parameter region or changing decision timing or feasibility semantics requires reoptimization under a redesigned model.
